articleTitle: Phylogeny Reconstruction of an Agricultural Crop Based on Nucleotide Sequence Homology Data Using a Genetic Algorithm
abstract: Phylogenetic analysis methods are widely used in the agro-industry to determine the level of divergence from type. Phylogeny allows us to establish a measure of similarity between homologous objects by reconstructing evolutionary history using tree topology based on data from specific regions of nucleotide sequences. There are widely used methods, such as, maximum likelihood and Bayes methods give different results on certain initial datasets of the same samples. This paper considers the genetic algorithm as an alternative method for phylogenetic tree construction. The paper considers a model of a modified genetic algorithm implemented as a program. Comparison in progress of maximum likelihood methods, Bayesian method and the proposed genetic algorithm on data with different homology of nucleotide sequences. The computational experiment using the genetic algorithm for phylogenetic reconstruction of the genus Triticum shows similar results for different sets of initial data, in contrast to other methods. Therefore, we can speak about the reliability of using this method for phylogeny.

articleTitle: Research on Selective Harmonic Elimination Pulse Width Modulation of Three-Level NPC Inverter Based on Adaptive Restart Genetic Algorithm
abstract: The harmonic elimination task of three-level neutral point clamped (3L-NPC) inverters is related to a complicated engineering optimization problem, which mainly involves constrained nonlinear transcendental equations with multiple solutions. In order to solve the problems of difficult initial value determination, slow convergence rates and susceptibility to local optima trapping in the process of using traditional numerical algorithms, This paper introduces a novel selective harmonic elimination pulse width modulation (SHEPWM) framework, enhanced by an adaptive restart genetic algorithm, to address the limitations of conventional optimization methods. By introducing the adaptive restart mechanism, the performance and robustness of the solution algorithm can be improved, so as to circumvent entrapment in local optima and secure the global optimum across the entire solution space. The simulation results show that there are divergent trends in the switching angles and the total harmonic distortion (THD) values of the output voltage obtained by the proposed method, but all of them can effectively eliminate the specified low-order harmonics. These findings verifies the practical applicability and solution diversity of the proposed method, as well as provides new ideas and methods for solving optimization problems in other engineering fields.

articleTitle: Experimental Research of the Robotic Assembly Process of Non-Rigid Cylindrical Parts Based on Positional-Force Control
abstract: Real-time intelligent algorithms for managing the assembly process remain key to this development in the technology of robotic assembly. The issue that has not yet widely gained scrutiny in regard to technological research and application is the robotic assembly of cylindrical, nonrigid pieces. The identification data from the force-torque sensor relies on some established mathematical models of the robotic assembly coupling phases. In this paper, a model is proposed that determines the effects of the assembly parameters during the mating step of the robotic assembly process. Process mode for assembling rigid sleeves on non-rigid shafts. For the experiment, the industrial robot IRB-140 was equipped with a Schunk force-torque sensor.

articleTitle: Approach for Task Transfer and Demonstration Learning Optimization in Industrial Robotic Manipulators
abstract: This paper proposes a refined method to enhance the performance and adaptability of industrial robotic manipulators by integrating demonstration learning with reinforcement learning, specifically using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). The approach starts with generating an initial trajectory through demonstration-based learning, which provides a robust foundation. Subsequently, PPO is employed to fine-tune the policy, improving precision while minimizing the amount of data required. Experimental evaluations reveal that our method achieves a 15% reduction in training data needs compared to standard approaches, along with enhanced adaptability across different tasks. This makes the method well-suited for flexible manufacturing settings where rapid task transfer is crucial.

articleTitle: Traffic Sign Recognition System Based on Neural Network Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of a system for automatic recognition of traffic signs using convolutional neural networks (CNN). The solution is based on the ResNet architecture with elements of recurrent layers, which increases the accuracy and versatility of image processing. Traffic sign recognition system provides user functionality to upload images of signs to the telegram bot, receive their classification, as well as useful tips on traffic rules. Development was performed using the PyTorch library, RTD dataset, and DeepPavlov language model. Test results showed high model accuracy (97.7% accuracy) and user-friendliness of the interface. The developed solution can be used both in educational institutions for driver training and as an auxiliary tool for analyzing the traffic situation.

articleTitle: Prediction of Online Social Network's Users Features and Social Behavior by Graph Neural Networks
abstract: In this work we developed and trained a machine learning models based on graph neural networks to predict some features as gender, age group, social behavior of VKontakte online social network users. As the input data for these models we used users' characteristics like different metrics, which represent quantitative data, and texts posted by user on his personal page, which represent a qualitative data. That is, in this work we solved the graph nodes' property prediction task. The performance of different graph neural network architectures based on GCN, SAGE, GAT, Transformer and GIN had been compared. The maximal performance had been obtained for Transformer based model, F1-score achieved 0.7809 in gender prediction, 0.7505 in age group prediction and 0.8008 in social behavior level prediction on test dataset.

articleTitle: Research on AI-Powered Employee Feedback Tools
abstract: This paper explores methods for employee feedback (EF) collection and introduces a new framework to improve the process. Current feedback collection process often suffers from slow workflow, bias, and poor Artificial Intelligence (AI) integration. Large Language Models (LLM) combined with human oversight may provide a more agile, objective, and user-friendly way for collecting and analyzing feedback. Existing EF tools were evaluated based on criteria such as AI capabilities, usability, and costs. Building on these findings, an open-source and self-hosted EF tool was developed. The tool integrates AI at every stage of the process and offers real-time AI assistance in writing, summarizing, and interpreting feedback. Pilot testing in two tech companies demonstrated user satisfaction.

articleTitle: Optimization of Micro-Object Identification with Factorization and Correction Mechanisms for Distorted Image Points
abstract: The scientific and methodological foundations for the optimal identification of micro-objects with mechanisms for using information structural components, features, statistical and dynamic characteristics of images have been developed. Mechanisms for tracking, detecting and correcting distorted points, factorizing the structural components of the image, filtering, segmentation, tracking distorted points under conditions of a priori insufficiency, parametric uncertainty, and low reliability of information processing are proposed. Methods for converting the initial brightness of a point into homogeneous objects as a function of two variables have been studied and nonlinear optimization functionals have been used. Mechanisms for factorization of the structural components of the image in the form of an indicator of linear connectivity, “neighborhood relationship” of three separate algorithms have been implemented. An alternative image factorization algorithm has been developed. A comparative analysis of effectiveness was carried out. The effectiveness of the mechanisms for detecting and correcting distorted points was studied using the criterion of the probability of undetected errors, the root-mean-square error, according to Shannon's estimates, the average level of intensity of the points, and the total compactness parameter. Rank estimates of integral indicators of image factorization were obtained for 30 images with 100 tests. A software package for visualization, recognition, and classification of images of microobjects has been developed, the implementations of which have been tested using real medical diagnostic data.

articleTitle: Prior Art Candidate Search on Base of Semantic Tree Analysis
abstract: The article discusses approaches to searching for analogous patents based on key phrase search, as well as by comparing semantic trees representing the component structure of a patented invention. Particular attention is paid to the use of graph databases, such as Neo4j, to represent complex relationships between components of patented devices. Approaches to searching for patent analogs based on key phrases are described. This method allows you to quickly identify relevant documents containing similar concepts in the form of text phrases. At the same time, comparing semantic trees provides a deeper analysis of the component structure of patents, including the relationships between their elements. The advantages of graph structures in the context of semantic information processing are considered, including their flexibility, scalability and the ability to identify hidden patterns. An example of constructing semantic trees and comparing them for two patents is given, illustrating the applicability of the method. As a result, it is shown that the combination of text search based on key phrases and analysis of graph representations of component structures of a patented invention allows to significantly increase the accuracy and efficiency of searching for patent analogues. This opens up new prospects for the development of intelligent data processing systems in the areas of patenting, artificial intelligence and big data analysis.

articleTitle: Neural Network Despeckling for Ultrasound Phased Diagnostics of Metallic Details
abstract: This paper describes the obtained original neural network architecture intended to process ultrasound images with fully developed speckle during phased diagnostics of metallic constructions and details. The proposed solution executes operations of convolution based on an autoencoder structure which is similar to the model U-Net. The suggested model incorporates a direct connection between the compressed and restored image, enabling dimensionality reduction while preserving fine details through skip connections. The results of modeling have shown that the proposed solution has an ability to both improve quality of the output image and detect real defects and filter artifacts masking for false defects.

articleTitle: A Short-Term Power Prediction Method for Wind Farm Cluster Based on Time Dynamic Graph Network and Improved Transformer Model
abstract: In recent years, wind power has gradually replaced thermal power as the main source of new energy generation. Wind power prediction in advance can help formulate scheduling strategies and improve the stability of the power system. With the advent of the Industry 4.0 and the widespread application of artificial intelligence technology, artificial algorithms have been extensively used in the field of wind power prediction. To further explore the spatiotemporal correlation of every wind farm in the wind farm cluster, a temporal dynamic graph network is used to divide the wind farm farm into several sub-clusters. Then, the KAN-BiLSTM-Transformer algorithm is used to predict wind power of each wind sub-cluster. Finally, the wind power of each sub-cluster is added to attain the final predicted power of the wind farm cluster. After verification, the RMSE and MAE of the proposed method is 0.06849 and 0.05805 respectively, with an accuracy of 93.15%, which is superior to the compared algorithms. Proposed method can provide more accurate prediction results.

articleTitle: Application of Sampling Algorithms for Sample Balancing in Diagnostics of Technical Object Condition
abstract: The paper proposes the use of sampling algorithms for the purpose of balancing the sample when diagnosing the condition of technical objects. The efficacy of a number of methods, including SMOTE, Tomek links, and ADASYN, is considered, as well as hybrid algorithms: TaS - a combination of Tomek links and SMOTE, and proposed by the authors new algorithm TaA - a combination of Tomek links and ADASYN. The support vector method is employed as the training model. The predictive quality of the models is evaluated using the F- score and A UC ROC metrics. In order to prevent the model from being fitted to achieve optimal predictive performance, cross-validation is conducted. The proposed methods are implemented as a software program written in the Python programming language. An analysis of the effectiveness of various sampling algorithms for sample balancing with the hydraulic system valve serving as a case study has been conducted. Three scenarios with disparate ratios of class imbalance, that is, the proportion of faulty conditions relative to serviceable ones, are examined. It is shown that the use of sampling methods enables balancing the sample and enhancing the values of quality metrics in predicting by approximately 30-40% in comparison to models that do not incorporate data balancing. This, in turn, facilitates the timely detection and warning of potential facility failures. The findings of the study indicate that hybrid data balancing techniques, such as TaS and TaA, are more efficacious than standalone methods, specifically, SMOTE, Tomek links, and ADASYN.

articleTitle: Development of a Tool Calibration Technique for Robotic Machining Using a Laser Tracker
abstract: The article presents a method for improving the accuracy of tool positioning for robotic machining using a laser tracker. The developed approach includes the construction of a local coordinate system of the instrument based on three labels, the determination of the position and orientation of the TCP point in space using matrix transformations, as well as algorithms for correcting the tool's trajectory. The features of tool calibration are described, including taking into account the overhang and angular position of the engraver. The experiments showed a decrease in the error of marking from 1.5 mm to 0.3 mm, which confirms the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The developed methodology and software can be used for robotic processing of complex and voluminous workpieces in various production conditions.

articleTitle: The Thermal Cutting Process of Flat Material on Figured Parts: Digital Twin Based on the Voxel Representation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to constructing a digital twin (DT) for the thermal cutting process of flat materials, such as those used in laser or gas cutting. The primary goal is to optimize the cutting tool path while accounting for thermal effects on the material, which can lead to overheating and deformation. The proposed method utilizes a discrete-logical (voxel-based) representation to model temperature changes in the material during cutting. A computational experiment demonstrates the effectiveness of the developed algorithm, which minimizes both idle travel and local overheating zones. The results show a 14% improvement in path optimization compared to traditional methods, highlighting the potential of integrating real-time temperature data into the cutting process. This approach enhances the quality of cut blanks and reduces production costs, making it a valuable tool for industrial applications.

articleTitle: Architecture of a Collaborative Robotic Complex with an Intelligent Control System
abstract: The article is devoted to increasing the degree of safety of collaborative robotic systems, taking into account the non-determinism of human behavior in the robot's work area. It is proposed to use an intelligent control system to increase the degree of safety and expand the functionality of the complex. A sensor subsystem has been developed, including a layout of its elements. A functional diagram of a collaborative robotic complex with an intelligent control system has been developed. The functions of the main elements of the control system are determined. A software structure has been developed that takes into account the distribution of software modules among computing devices. The functions of each of the software modules and the types of information transferred between the software modules are described.

articleTitle: Overview of Digital Solutions to Improve Operational Efficiency and Reduce Emissions for Coal-Fired Thermal Power Plants
abstract: In Vietnam, many energy sources are currently in operation, such as thermal power, hydropower, biomass power, solar power, wind power, etc. However, thermal power still accounts for a large and important part of the power system. In particular, these thermal power plants burn fossil fuels like coal. To ensure the operational efficiency of thermal power plants while reducing emissions and contributing to Vietnam's roadmap to achieving net zero by 2050, it is essential to address the fluctuations in coal resources that are not as originally designed. This situation poses many challenges for thermal power plants in Vietnam. It requires a comprehensive solution to control and evaluate the entire operational process in the plant, especially in the boiler area, which determines key factors such as efficiency, reliability, and emissions of the plant.

articleTitle: Psychological Profiling of Users Based on Social Media Data Analysis Using the BERT Model
abstract: The article deals with the problem of automated construction of psychological portrait of social network users using machine learning and neural networks methods. In the conditions of the modern labour market, effective human resource management requires fast and accurate profiling of candidates. Traditional methods of personality analysis require significant time and human resources, which makes the process time-consuming and not always prompt. The importance of psychoanalysis for human resource management is substantiated and the methodology of using MBTI typology as a tool for classifying personality characteristics is presented. The authors analyze modern research in the field of automated psychological profiling and consider the use of machine learning to analyze the texts of social network users. The paper presents the methodology of data collection and processing using APIs of social platforms, as well as the application of algorithms based on the MBTI model. Special attention is paid to the BERT method, which allows taking into account the context of words and providing high classification accuracy. The results of the study demonstrate high accuracy of personality type classification, reaching 97.72%, which confirms the effectiveness of the automated approach to profiling. The use of the developed model significantly reduces the analysis time and increases its predictive power. In the future, this area may become an important tool for HR-specialists, allowing them to optimize the recruitment process and analyze the personality characteristics of candidates.

articleTitle: Intelligent Monitoring of Complex Technical Systems: Application of the Forecast Aggregation Approach
abstract: The paper presents a description of an approach to intelligent analysis of the state of complex technical systems. The approach includes extracting time series from technical system logs and determining abnormal values based on forecasting results. An aggregation method for obtaining a forecast using a neural network is used. A conclusion is made about the state of the object's characteristics by integrating the results of anomaly detection and knowledge about the subject area from the OVL ontology as a result of the analysis. The proposed approach is implemented in an information system. Experiments were conducted on hardware storage system data. The approach has proven its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Alternative Protection of Electrical Installations
abstract: The paper presents the principle of operation of the developed maximum current protection, the purpose of which is to protect high-voltage electrical installations from short circuits. The presented protection is performed without using current relays and current transformers (CT) with ferromagnetic cores (including those built into the circuit breaker) widely used in the electric power industry, which have a large weight and dimensional parameters, as well as high cost in comparison with magnetosensitive elements such as reed switches. The proposed protection is made with the use of reed switches. Current protections of electrical installations with the use of reed switches can be used at the moment only as a duplicate to traditional protections, as there is no their wide introduction into production and experience of operation of such protections, i.e. statistical data on these protections are required. At the same time it should be said that such protections are not inferior to traditional protections in terms of speed. The presented protection characterizes an innovative approach in the implementation of relay protection and has the effect of resource-saving materials. The proposed maximum current protection is performed in the form of a device, with its installation inside the circuit breaker located in the cell of a closed switchgear (switchgear) with a voltage equal to 35 kV.

articleTitle: Wheelchair Wheel Design with Transformable “Wheel-Leg” Configuration for Climbing Stairs and Various Surfaces
abstract: The dynamic and uneven terrain of our environment introduces complexity for locomotion vehicles to navigate easily across different settings. Wheelchairs belong to the category of vehicles that require locomotion across various uneven terrains, such as stairs and other partitions. Therefore, the aim of this work is to design a wheel that can travel through various environments without using complex mechanisms. This aim was achieved by creating a novel transformable wheel. This wheel can turn into a legged wheel without using a complex mechanism and, when unnecessary, transform back into a normal wheel. Several simulations were carried out to understand the design's capability to overcome obstacles. In this case, the stair was the obstacle, and the results illustrated that the wheel is capable of climbing stairs without serious issues. Different parameters, such as speed and force, were examined with various values. The results showed that the weight on the wheelchair plays a significant role in climbing. For instance, with lighter weight, the structure moves without major slipping. The roughness of the surface is also related to the wheelchair's ability to reach the top of the stairs. A finer depth of cuts on the surface of the stairs increases the chance of the legged wheel firmly gripping and moving up the stairs.

articleTitle: Optimization and Improvement of Reliability of Machine Learning Algorithms Based on Regularization Methods
abstract: Nowadays, optimizing the results of machine learning algorithms is of great importance in the field of artificial intelligence. This article analyzes the effectiveness of Lasso, Ridge, and Elastic Net regression methods to increase the reliability of the results of machine learning algorithms in assessing economic indicators. These methods help to eliminate the problems of overfitting and multicollinearity, and are aimed at improving models based on machine learning algorithms. The study tests the effectiveness of these methods on a data set of economic indicators, and uses the Grid Search method to determine the optimal values for model parameters. As a result, it is shown that these approaches can improve the accuracy and generalizability of economic indicator assessments.

articleTitle: Toward the Use of Permanent Magnets Consisting of Several Cylindrical Segments in Magnetostrictive Transducers of Displacements on Ultrasonic Torsion Waves
abstract: The article is devoted to issue of possible replacement ring permanent magnets in magnetostrictive transducers linear or angular displacements, used also in robotics, by construction from non-magnetic material of same shape and parameters, containing several permanent magnets of cylindrical shape. The elements of basic design acoustic path magnetostrictive transducer linear displacements and known mathematical models of processes excitation, translation and reading of analog output signal are analyzed. The forms of permanent magnets used in magnetostrictive displacement transducers and mathematical models used for modeling and calculations magnetic fields formed by permanent magnets are considered in detail. Investigations of magnetic fields formed by several cylindrical shaped segments are performed. Computational experiments to investigate dependence of projection total magnetic field strength created by segments on 0Z axis on z coordinate, as well as computational experiments to investigate strength in center of structure made of non-magnetic material allowed us to draw conclusions about possibility of replacing the ring permanent magnet with structure including several permanent magnets of cylindrical shape. Also, results of computational experiments have shown necessity of taking into account the distance between segments, increase of which contributes to sharp decrease in the amplitude total value of magnetic field strength. It is noted that possible replacement of ring permanent magnets by several segments of cylindrical shape allows not only to obtain required for excitation of ultrasonic wave of total value magnetic field strength, but also in general to reduce the cost of magnetostrictive transducers of linear displacements, used including in robotics.

articleTitle: Optimal Control of a Delayed Model for an Industrial Robot Manipulator
abstract: The problem of controlling an industrial manipulator with time delays in the control system is considered. A bilinear model for the single-link manipulator is investigated. The control torque of the actuator is formed using regulators with an aftereffect from the beginning of the movement to the current moment. The task of optimal control of the manipulator is to determine the admissible control that minimizes the functional describing the deviation of the manipulator movement angle from the specified position. The functional and the control correspond to the Bellman equation. The problem of synthesizing the optimal control of the single-link manipulator is reduced to finding a solution to a system of differential equations that satisfies the boundary conditions at the ends of the control interval.

articleTitle: Remote Monitoring Device for Gas Leakage
abstract: Due to the widespread installation of gas equipment in private homes, the likelihood of emergencies related to gas leaks has increased. Accordingly, the task arose of taking measures to prevent accidents and dangerous situations. For this purpose, new specialized devices based on gas sensors and innovative monitoring and notification tools are currently being used and developed. They detect the leak and report the threat to the control post using a dedicated communication channel. At the same time, the availability and accessibility of such devices is very limited. In this regard, there is an urgent task to develop an affordable gas leak detection system for widespread use in the industrial and civil sectors. In this article, a variant of the gas leak control system using wireless technologies and cloud data processing is proposed. At the same time, the functionality and accessibility of the proposed solution is based on the concept of devices for Internet of Things systems and gas sensors. It is important to note that the Internet of Things systems make it possible to increase the availability of mass adoption of devices due to lower requirements for the end device and increases reliability through real-time monitoring. The developed sensor was tested within the framework of the stated scenarios and showed the effectiveness of its implementation in existing Smart Home and Industry 4.0 systems.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Control of an Unmanned Flying Platform Carrier
abstract: This article examines the problem of controlling the flight of an unmanned flying platform-carrier (UFPC), carrying a group of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) on its upper surface. The flying platform delivers a group of UAVs to a given point in space at the desired time for an air launch from its upper surface. For a more complete picture of the control object, a brief description of the UFPC with the UAVs located on it is given. A detailed description of the mathematical model (MM) of the movement of an unmanned flying platform-carrier is given. In addition, a detailed description of the components of forces and moments included in the mathematical model is given. Nonlinear control laws for an unmanned aerial platform carrier have been synthesized. For the synthesis, a mathematical model of the spatial motion of the UFPC was used. The ADAR method, the analytical design of aggregated regulators, was chosen as the synthesis method. Detailed procedures for the synthesis of nonlinear control laws using the ADAR method are given. As a result of the synthesis, a closed nonlinear system “control object - controller” was obtained for various flight modes of a flying platform-carrier of unmanned aerial vehicles. In the process of modeling, it was found that the closed nonlinear system is asymptotically stable throughout the entire operational range of flight modes, and the resulting controllers ensure the fulfillment of the assigned control tasks.

articleTitle: Automation Methods of Data Collection and Analysis for Managing Complex IT Infrastructures
abstract: The article discusses an approach to the organization of monitoring and management of server equipment, aimed at ensuring the stable operation of the IT infrastructure. Modern methods based on threshold analysis cannot cope with the volume and variety of data, which requires automation of the collection, processing and analysis of metrics. A computing cluster of servers using the Proxmox VE virtualization platform is presented as an object of research. The features of time series storage and data processing using the InfluxDB database, which has a convenient query language called Flux, are described. Implemented software architecture for integrating monitoring and data analysis tools, including Prometheus PVE Exporter, Telegraf and Flux. The advantages of using Python for metric analysis and query development using the Builder pattern are shown, which simplifies working with the system. Methods of data preprocessing and visualization for anomaly analysis and forecasting with the aim of maintaining the stable operation of server equipment are discussed. The proposed approach ensures the efficiency and ease of monitoring, while also enhancing the accuracy of decision-making given the increasing complexity of IT infrastructure.

articleTitle: Methods and Software Tools for Converting Road Marking Line Segmentation Mask to Object Representation for Highly Automated Vehicles
abstract: This paper describes the development of an algorithm for converting segmentation masks derived from neural networks into ordered sets of point coordinates representing road markings for highly automated vehicles (HAVs). Several methods are considered, including the nearest neighbor method, polynomial approximation, Hough transform, and parallel contouring. Performance tests and complexity analyses are performed for each method. The parallel contour method with dynamic search for opposite points was the most effective, demonstrating linear complexity and high accuracy in approximating road marking contours. This solution ensures efficient processing of large real-time datasets, critical for HAV navigation. The study integrates the algorithm into a unified system, combining segmentation with mask-to-line conversion, enhancing autonomous driving precision.

articleTitle: The Influence of Shielding Enclosure on the Characteristics of Protection Devices Operating in Differential and Common Modes
abstract: In this work, we used quasi-static simulation to evaluate the influence of shielding enclosure on the attenuation coefficient and per-unit-length delays of devices protecting against ultra-wideband pulses. The protection devices were 6-and 8-conductor structures, each consisting of two transmission lines with inhomogeneous dielectric filling, combined into one structure. The simulation showed that increasing the distance between the shield walls and the 6-conductor structure resulted in the same attenuation coefficients as without the shield. Therefore, the shield should be kept as far away as possible to preserve the characteristics. In the 8-conductor structure, increasing the distance to the shield walls had a non-significant influence on the attenuation coefficient in the common and differential modes. This probably happened because the active conductors were placed in the central part (inside) of the structure cross-section. The per-unit-length mode delays in both structures were not influenced by changing distances to the walls.

articleTitle: Simulation and Automated Temperature Control of the Supercomputer Center
abstract: High computational load on supercomputers and data centers is accompanied by excessive energy consumption and critical heating of electronic units. The temperature field on the electronic units in the server room was simulated using a finite element engineering program. The dependence of temperature on external conditions was calculated and the need to include additional air conditioning in the server room was shown. Efficient operation and further increase in the productivity of server rooms require constant monitoring of their temperature fields and cooling systems. This paper describes the results of developing an application for monitoring the temperature in a supercomputer center in order to automate high temperature warning system, which is especially important during the hot summer period. Previously used systems can trigger local alarms, but do not have remote notification capabilities such as email or SMS, and require manual adjustment. The proposed application is aimed at improving operational safety by providing engineers with the ability to receive alerts directly to their phones, which allows for better control and management of the temperature in server rooms. The combination of a computer model that can simulate the temperature field and a monitoring system that measures temperature makes it possible to create a digital twin of a supercomputer center.

articleTitle: Using Fuzzy Bio-Inspired Algorithms for Quality Management of Science-Intensive Products
abstract: The key way to improve the quality of science-intensive products produced on technological lines that are part of multi-stage production chains is to optimize the design, operation and reengineering of technological processes. High computational complexity, caused by the need to process large volumes of multidimensional data and take into account many time and resource constraints, determines the feasibility of using metaheuristic methods capable of finding close to optimal solutions to algorithmically complex tasks in an acceptable time. The article proposes a new approach to solving tasks of optimizing the composition and operating modes of technological lines, based on the integrated use of swarm intelligence and fuzzy logic. Algorithms inspired by the collective behavior of swimming fish and bacteria were used to solve structural and parametric optimization tasks. Their hybridization with fuzzy logic methods has made it possible to increase the convergence of optimization algorithms by significantly reducing the search space.

articleTitle: Research and Development of an Early Fire Warning System for Ships Using Artificial Neural Networks
abstract: Fire has become a serious threat to both human life and the natural environment. Traditional fire alarm systems often face challenges during deployment, especially in large areas or with complex terrain. Some methods of detecting fire risks apply artificial intelligence integrated into intelligent fire alarm systems on shore. In addition, the application of artificial intelligence on modern ships is increasingly popular for many purposes, such as enhancing maritime safety and minimizing accidents and risks during operations at sea. This paper studies and tests an early fire warning system based on Artificial Neural Network (ANN) to minimize damage related to fires on ships. The system combines temperature, humidity, and Carbon Monoxide (CO) and Carbon Dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) sensors, all collected through a microcontroller. The environmental data collected from these sensors is processed and analyzed using a predictive model built in MATLAB. The research results demonstrate that the model achieves high accuracy and provides rapid response, significantly reducing the time required to detect potential fire hazards and thus minimizing damage.

articleTitle: Parameter Estimation of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles Dynamics. A Data-Driven Optimization Framework
abstract: Accurate parameter estimation in ship dynamics models is pivotal for enhancing navigation precision, optimizing control systems, and ensuring maritime safety. This study explores two distinct methodologies: the “Grey Box” approach, where the governing equations of ship dynamics are known but certain parameters remain unidentified, and the “Black Box” approach, which relies entirely on trajectory data without any prior knowledge of the underlying mathematical models. Leveraging machine learning techniques, specifically Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, alongside optimization algorithms like L-BFGS-B, this research aims to evaluate and compare the efficacy of both approaches in estimating model parameters and predicting ship trajectories. The findings demonstrate that while the Grey Box approach benefits from incorporating physical laws for parameter tuning, the Black Box method offers flexibility in modeling complex, nonlinear dynamics purely based on empirical data. The integrated use of these methodologies provides a robust framework for enhancing the accuracy and reliability of ship dynamics models, contributing significantly to maritime engineering applications.

articleTitle: Automated System for Processing Initial Data on Electrical Loads in Multi-Apartment Residential Buildings
abstract: The statistical analysis of electricity consumption in multifamily residential buildings was conducted to justify the values of specific loads for these buildings. The foundation for this analysis was the daily profiles of electricity consumption. Given the limited ability to obtain a large number of electricity consumption profiles for multifamily residential buildings, the approach adopted involved determining the values of specific loads based on parameters from private samples of the overall population of the multifamily building. Subsequently, statistical processing of the daily power profiles was conducted for each cluster of the multifamily building based on the obtained representative samples. To process the initial data on electricity consumption in the apartments of the multifamily building, a program was developed using the R programming language for statistical data processing and graphical work. The functioning of this program utilized the pre-installed “R” version 4.1.1, along with the installed database server “Firebird” version 2.5.9. The primary programming language for the program “Complex for Automated Processing of Initial Data on Electrical Loads of Multifamily Residential Buildings” is Delphi. The development environment and compiler used is Embarcadero® Delphi 11. The main function of the program is to calculate the key parameters of specific power for the apartments in the multifamily building, processing the initial data on electricity consumption to assess their specific electrical power.

articleTitle: Human Silhouette Visualization System Using CSI Data
abstract: This work aims to understand how a person can influence the propagation of electromagnetic waves in a wireless transmission medium in order to determine his location and visualization. The parameters analyzed in this work were the values of the phases and amplitudes of the signal for 9 pairs of antennas and 56 suborthogonal subcarriers. The article proposes an algorithm that converts the original data into an image with a human silhouette. The images obtained after the algorithm can be used as an auxiliary tool for security alarms. This algorithm does not violate the fact of confidentiality, which is an advantage compared to conventional video surveillance. This algorithm can visualize a person's silhouette with an accuracy of more than 88% on a small amount of training data.

articleTitle: Toward the Use of a Block of Two Planar Spiral Solenoids in High-Temperature Magnetostrictive Sensors Based on Torsional Waves
abstract: Today, high-temperature linear displacement sensors are in demand in rocket and space technology, as part of the reactor compartments of nuclear power plant units, for measuring the position of a turbine servomotor, and for determining the position of electric arc furnace electrodes in the steel industry. Magnetostrictive sensors of linear displacements are the most suitable for these tasks, but their application is limited by the used materials with low Curie point and the use of coil products in the design. Therefore, the actual task is to create high-temperature magnetostrictive displacement sensors capable of operating at ambient temperatures up to +600 °C, while maintaining the stability and accuracy of measurements. In order to achieve the set objectives, the use of a design containing two planar solenoids located on ceramic substrates is proposed. The use of a unit consisting of two planar solenoids al-lows to summarize the output signals formed by each of the solenoids and contributes to the in-crease in the amplitude of the output signal. In addition, this design also allows to obtain a difference signal, which can be used for more complex processing of the measurement signal. Computational experiments and experimental verification were carried out to investigate the amplitude and shape of the output signal when changing the parameters of the solenoids and the distance between them. The experimental studies have fully confirmed the results of theoretical studies and computational experiments. The experimental studies fully confirmed the results of theoretical studies and computation-al experiments.

articleTitle: Cloud Removal in Satellite Images Using a Generative Adversarial Approach
abstract: Automation of a wide range of operations in the agro-industrial sector at the current stage of technology development involves the application of advanced solutions in electronics, biotechnology, and information technologies. One of the directions of process optimization in agriculture is the introduction of information systems functioning on the basis of satellite imagery data analysis. To improve the efficiency of satellite data application, it is advisable to use machine learning and artificial intelligence methods. Satellite data allow monitoring a set of indicators describing chemical and physical characteristics, soil types, weather conditions, humidity. These indicators play an important role in the decision-making process of smart farming systems. The indicators are available in the form of satellite images, the quality of which depends on many factors. In order to apply such images in agricultural information systems, it is necessary to perform deep image analysis and cleaning. The approach aimed at applying a generative deep neural network to clean satellite images from clouds and shadows is proposed. The approach is based on training the neural network on synthesized data.

articleTitle: Multi-Criteria Model for Assessing the Effectiveness of Monitoring Parameters of Automated Process Control Systems
abstract: The article is devoted to a multi-criteria model for assessing informative parameters at control points of an industrial system. The results of calculations of the proposed model help to make decisions on the need to improve the parameters of monitoring system segments. Methods for collecting control data from an automated process control system and methods for obtaining several weighted characteristics for each process parameter are described. These characteristics show the importance of the parameter from one of the points of view. Based on these, the total weight of information content for all parameters is calculated. Total weight is then used to decide the need to improve the collection of control data from the automated process control system for each of the system zones. Some possible improvements to the proposed model are also suggested.

articleTitle: On the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Cybersecurity Incident Investigations
abstract: The increasing number of cyber threats significantly complicates the investigation of information security incidents. Traditional digital forensic methods face challenges due to the growing volume of data and the increasing sophistication of cyberattacks. This paper presents a decision-support algorithm designed to assist specialists in conducting efficient and accurate investigations using artificial intelligence techniques. The proposed algorithm incorporates anomaly detection, attacker behavior modeling, and intelligent digital evidence analysis, thereby enhancing the effectiveness of forensic investigations. Furthermore, the developed solution can be further integrated with SIEM systems and digital forensic tools, enabling automated threat correlation and accelerating incident response. The use of AI-driven analytics improves investigation accuracy, reduces the risk of human errors, and optimizes forensic processes in modern cybersecurity environments.

articleTitle: Installing and Configuring Windows Subsystem for Linux in Cloud Computing
abstract: There are several approaches for the joint (simultaneous) operation of several different operating systems on the same computer. These are load managers, virtual machines, emulation systems. Until recently, the main way was to use VMware virtual machines, Virtual Box, etc. However, these systems did not fully support all the features of the Linux OS and were quite heavy, having low compatibility and speed. Virtual machines have completely captured the server configuration market, allowing one to deploy multiple versions of Linux, Windows server, etc. on one physical server. Microsoft's leading software developer has lagged far enough in this area by offering its own Hyper-V hypervisor only in Windows Server 2008. Currently, Microsoft in the new versions of Windows 10 and 11 offered the fastest and most convenient method of integrating Windows and Linux - Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL). This system supports system calls on Linux and allows one to develop full-fledged programs for Linux on the same computer with Windows. In this article, we consistently review the steps of installing WSL in various versions of Windows, offering solutions to the problems that arise, since this task turned out to be quite non-trivial on non-new hardware and not Windows 11. We are considering ways to install the system on various hardware configurations and Windows versions. As a result, we get conclusions about the effectiveness of the chosen approach compared to the VMware virtual machine.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Effectiveness of Ensemble Methods in Solving Multi-Class Classification Problems
abstract: In this research work, ensemble methods for analyzing classification problems were analyzed. Currently, various methods and algorithms are proposed and implemented based on machine systems to increase the accuracy of results. In this study, XGBoost, Random Forest, LightGBM, and AdaBoost algorithms were applied, and their results were evaluated based on model performance criteria including Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1-score. The research results showed that the XGBoost model achieved better results than ensemble models, which achieved a 92% accuracy result. This confirms its potential for widespread application in the field of medical diagnostics. High results were also achieved with the LightGBM and AdaBoost algorithms. LightGBM and AdaBoost showed high recall performance. Ensemble methods possess higher accuracy compared to traditional classifiers and help effectively address issues related to data class imbalance characteristics. The results of this research demonstrate that ensemble methods provide high reliability and adaptability in multi-class classification problems. The research results confirm the high effectiveness of ensemble methods in the process of early diagnosis and prediction of diabetes mellitus. This suggests that it could be applied to detect other diseases in the future.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of Combined Actuator for Rehabilitation Exoskeleton
abstract: This paper deals with the mathematical modeling of a lower limb rehabilitation exoskeleton with a combined actuator. The actuator consists of an electric actuator and a mechanical energy storage spring acting as a gravity compensator, which is used to create an auxiliary torque compensating part of the gravity load. A mathematical model is described and mathematical modeling of the trajectory motion of the leg of the exoskeleton with a combined drive under different characteristics of the mechanical energy storage is carried out. The trajectory motion is based on anthropomorphic gait, based on approximated data of human step video recordings. The simulation results confirm that the mechanical energy storage generates an auxiliary torque compensating part of the gravitational forces of the exoskeleton leg.

articleTitle: Approach for Analyzing the Performance of 5G Networks During the Initial Planning Phase Without Deployment Using the NS-3 Network Simulator
abstract: This study aims to enhance the performance of fifth-generation (5G) wireless networks. The research involves analyzing existing approaches to the design and deployment of 5G infrastructure, as well as conducting simulation experiments using current network configurations. These experiments will provide insights into key parameters of 5G systems and enable the evaluation of their performance at the preliminary planning stage, thereby reducing risks and improving the accuracy of network deployment. This approach will facilitate more efficient network planning, particularly for industrial Internet of Things (IoT) applications. Optimizing 5G networks for industrial needs will unlock advanced capabilities such as real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance, and seamless integration of equipment and devices. This, in turn, will support Industry 4.0 initiatives, enhancing productivity and boosting the competitiveness of industrial enterprises.

articleTitle: Software Platform for Analyzing the State of Storage Systems Using Hybrid Intelligent Algorithms
abstract: The article presents a description of the developed software platform that provides automation of data storage server state monitoring using a hybrid algorithm. The developed algorithm combines an ontological approach and machine learning elements. A comparative assessment of various approaches was carried out: cluster analysis, autoencoders, LSTM, fuzzy ontologies and hybrid models - when analyzing methods for searching for anomalies in time series. The hybrid evaluation model showed the best results for all criteria. It was chosen to develop a prototype of the software platform. Experiments were conducted on hardware storage system data. The software platform proved its effectiveness in solving the problem.

articleTitle: Effects of Simulator Fidelity on Automated Vehicle Object Perception Accuracy
abstract: The development of intelligent transportation systems, and intelligent vehicles in particular, requires significant time and effort, with one of the primary phases being the training of the automated driving system. This training can be conducted using real-world annotated data or within a simulation environment. Simulation tools can provide a wide array of traffic scenarios unavailable in the real world. However, simulator development is complex and time-consuming, necessitating numerous compromises throughout the process. Among these challenges is the effects of graphical fidelity, which encompasses the level of detail and image resolution, on object detection accuracy in automated vehicles. This article aims to determine the importance of simulator graphical fidelity for automated vehicle development and define guidelines for simulator fidelity requirements. CARLA simulator was used to collect images for the AV control and object detection system. Experiments show that increasing image resolution while maintaining a constant level of detail leads to a decreasing improvement in model accuracy, and reducing image quality does not lead to a significant loss in object detection accuracy. It is also shown that graphical fidelity should be balanced with budget and computational constraints. It is concluded that in AV simulation, the priority should not be the pursuit of maximal graphical fidelity but rather the focus on the accuracy of traffic participant behavior, dynamics, and interactions.

articleTitle: Development of a State Machine for Trust Assessment in Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: This paper discusses the use of state machines for analyzing and evaluating the stability of cyber-physical systems. The focus is on typical system architecture, including a high-level control layer, a network layer, a low-level control layer, and a physical layer. Key factors affecting flight stability, such as aerodynamic performance, control systems and external influences, are investigated. Developed metrics for stability analysis to help quantify the state of the system and identify potential problems. An important part of the work is the final assessment of the condition of the machine, which integrates the results of all previous stages of analysis, allowing for a consistent and justified assessment. The experimental study conducted within the framework of this work confirms the effectiveness of the proposed approach, showing that the use of state machines can significantly improve the quality of flight [1] stability assessment. The results of the study have practical implications for the development of more robust cyber-physical systems.

articleTitle: An Approach Based on Data Profiling at the Preparing a Dataset for Cleaning
abstract: It is known that today the volume of data is increasing dramatically in every field. This in turn complicates the process of data analysis. In this case, creating a data profile facilitates big data analysis. Therefore, data profiling is becoming an important and integral part of data analysis necessary for making accurate decisions in various fields. The importance of data profiling is that during the data profiling process, data that leads to incorrect decisions is identified and eliminated. After going through this process, the dataset becomes fully ready for data cleaning. The probability of algorithms built on the basis of a properly organized data cleaning data set to produce accurate and effective results increases several times. This research paper reveals the importance of data profiling in data analytics and artificial intelligence algorithms. At the same time, information is provided about the sequence of practical work performed in the data profiling process. The experimental dataset is also subjected to data profiling and the data cleaning processes to be performed on this selected dataset are determined. The article concludes with the main conclusions of this research work.

articleTitle: The System of Formation of the Flight Task of the Aircraft for the Purpose of Processing Agricultural Land
abstract: This paper describes a software module created for the purpose of forming a flight task with controls for the cultivation of agricultural land. The problem of effective treatment of territories with various chemicals in order to increase yields is relevant at this point in time, as evidenced by the statistics of companies in this field of activity. The module performs the functions of not only forming a task, but also provides recommendations for the implementation of the maximum productivity of the sprayer drone when moving around the territory. In this case, the recommendations are understood as a number of functional features that indirectly affect the formation of the flight task by the user, for example, the software module provides the ability to calculate the actual area of contact of the working fluid on the ground surface, taking into account such factors as wind speed and direction, as well as the flight altitude of the aircraft. Another important feature of the module design is the provided scalability of the system with additional functions, which is also important when creating an integrated control system for a robotic system.

articleTitle: The Use of Digital Twin Technology in the Development of Intelligent Equipment
abstract: The article discusses the impact and significance of digital twin technology in the development of intelligent equipment within the manufacturing sector. It explains how digital twins create virtual replicas of physical assets, processes, or systems, allowing for real-time monitoring and analysis. The article highlights the benefits of using digital twins, such as enhanced decision-making, proactive maintenance, and improved operational efficiency through predictive analytics. Additionally, it emphasizes the role of digital twins in fostering innovation by enabling manufacturers to simulate various scenarios without risk. As industries move toward automation and smart manufacturing practices, the article underscores the importance of digital twins in adapting to changing market demands and driving continuous improvement. Ultimately, it portrays digital twin technology as a key enabler for the future of intelligent equipment development and industrial innovation.

articleTitle: Self-Attention Based Approach to Iris Segmentation
abstract: This research investigates the integration of advanced self-attention techniques into deep neural network architectures, focusing on accurately segmenting the iris and pupil regions in infrared imagery. We propose modified variants of non-local block self-attention modules, tailored to enhance the self-attentive capabilities of the model while addressing the unique properties of infrared imaging data. Through these custom modifications, we achieved notable enhancements in the model's segmentation accuracy. Extensive testing was conducted using a well-curated infrared image dataset, confirming the robustness of the proposed approach. These findings open new avenues for advancements in infrared image processing, enabling diverse applications in fields ranging from biometrics to surveillance. Furthermore, this work demonstrates the potential of specialized self-attention mechanisms to significantly elevate the performance of deep learning models when applied to niche imaging challenges.

articleTitle: The Phenomenon of Digital Mediation: The Perceptual Landscape Mediated by the Writer's Digital Twin
abstract: The paper presents a consideration of the use of the “digital twin” technology in philological research discourse. The integration of the digital twin concept into the problematics of linguistic personality studies allows us to observe the semantic-functional distribution of the latter in the communicative binomial “real reality - virtual reality”. The digital twin assumes the mission of a technological mediator, thus establishing and controlling the relationship between language, meaning and structures of experience. The ongoing research actualizes the issues of communicative and speech quality of digital functional models, their style identity to the object of digital modeling, which is considered to be the writer's individual-author's writing or the embodied hermeneutic writer's technique.

articleTitle: Organization of Storage and Processing of Experimental Results from the Continuous Process of Styrene-Butadiene Copolymerization Using Databases
abstract: The article presents an approach to storing and processing the results of industrial, laboratory, and computational experiments based on databases. The approach is presented on the example of the process of copolymerization of butadiene with styrene, which proceeds continuously in a cascade of series-connected ideal mixing reactors. A conceptual and logical database model of the industrial process under study has been created. The constructed structure can be adapted for other copolymerization processes, depending on the type of process, its formulation, and the process flow conditions. The presented physical model is implemented as a database and has been tested in the Microsoft SQL Server environment.

articleTitle: The Dataset for a Machine Learning Forecast Model of an Overhead Power Lines Icing
abstract: The problem of overhead power line phase conductors and ground wire icing is currently very strong. While the climate is changing, the line icing forecast become less accurate. The periods of strong icing changes and even the regions that were not considered as dangerous for lines icing are facing a “new” problem for grids. The ice is dangerous for an overhead power line and is a consequence of the stability of a power system. There are several measures to prevent and control ice damage to a powerline conductor. But the first step of using these measures and instruments is icing forecast in time and location. The article presents the approach for using a machine learning algorithm and dataset collection to accurately forecast ice on power line phase conductors and ground wires. The aim of research is to collect the dataset and research accuracy in forecasting the ice formation without special sensors. The results demonstrate a satisfactory level of performance the accuracy of approximately 81% on the test set that are satisfying and may be testing on a real grid.

articleTitle: Resource-Saving Protection of Electrical Installations with Inductive Coils
abstract: It is worth noting that a key challenge in today's electric power systems relates to the implementation of relay protection for high-voltage electrical installations. This practice has been a topic of discussion at several international conferences on large power systems (CIGRE). It has been suggested that the use of traditional current transformers (CTs) with ferromagnetic cores in such contexts may be a concern. These devices are known for their intensive use of metal, their substantial size, and the cost of their insulation. This article proposes a novel approach to current protection for electrical installations, utilising inductance coils as a means to illustrate the concept. The selection of inductance coils is predicated on their numerous advantages over other magnetosensitive elements in terms of relay protection. However, the feasibility of employing these coils for current protection in various electrical installations has not yet been thoroughly examined. This paper aims to address these concerns in the context of developing current protection for electrical installations using inductance coils fed from complete switchgear (CSG) with voltages ranging from 6 to 10 kV. The proposed protection facilitates the adjustment of settings through remote manipulation of the inductance coil, relative to the plane of the current-carrying busbar, utilising a micromotor. It is hoped that the elimination of costly and metal-intensive current transformers with ferromagnetic cores will contribute to reduced material expenses for the construction of current protection for electrical installations of any type and voltage class.

articleTitle: Determining Strong Connectivity Method of Periodic Fuzzy Graph for Decision Analysis in Emergency Situations
abstract: This paper considers the problem of analysing the evacuation territory in the case where the model of this territory can be represented by a periodic fuzzy graph. For this purpose, the paper introduces the concept of a fuzzy set of strong connectivity of a periodic fuzzy graph, that is, a graph in which elements (vertices) are in fuzzy relationships. Moreover, these relations change in discrete time and have the property of periodicity. We propose a method for finding a strongly connected fuzzy set. An example of finding it is considered. A strongly connected fuzzy set can serve as a basis for choosing a movement strategy during evacuation, when the territory model is represented by a periodic fuzzy graph.

articleTitle: Generating Digital Models Using Text-to-3D and Image-to-3D Prompts: Critical Case Study
abstract: In the world of technology and AI, digital models play an important role in our lives and are an essential part of the digital twins of real-world objects. They can be created by designers, artists, or game developers using spline curves and surfaces, meshes, and voxels, but making such models is too time-consuming. With the growth of AI tools, there is interest in the automated generation of 3D models, such as generative design approaches, which can save creators valuable time. This paper reviews several online 3D model generators and critically analyses the results, hoping to see higher-quality results from different prompts.

articleTitle: The Use of the Integral Method to Compare the Efficiency of Neural Networks to Improve Image Resolution Depending on Size and Format Using the Example of Road Photos
abstract: Roads occupy one of the most important places in the life of a modern person. The quality of the road surface is its key characteristic. To assess the quality of roads, there are many different systems that mainly solve the problem using image analysis. For better work with photos, they are preprocessed. Preprocessing, for example, includes changing the image resolution, which can be implemented using machine learning methods, including the use of neural networks. In this paper, a comparative analysis of the neural networks efficiencies to improve image resolution, depending on size and format, using the integral method is carried out. The neural networks selected are EDSR, ESPCN, ESRGAN, FSRCNN, LapSRN. The research material consists of road surface images in 5 sizes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{100}\times \mathbf{100}, \mathbf{141}\times \mathbf{141},\ \mathbf{173}\times \mathbf{173},\ \mathbf{200}\times \mathbf{200},\ \mathbf{224}\times \mathbf{224})$</tex> and 3 formats (bmp, jpg, png). All neural networks have a linear O(n) dependence of the average time to obtain an improved image version on the photo size for each format. EDSR, ESPCN, FSRCNN, LapSRN also have a linear O(n) dependence for the average allocated memory on the size for all formats. ESRGAN has a constant O(1) dependence on the allocated memory for jpg and png formats, and almost constant dependence for bmp. ESPCN has the best time efficiency, and ESRGAN has the best space efficiency. ESRGAN and ESPCN also have the best integral efficiency values.

articleTitle: Overhead Lines Online Monitoring Using in the Condition Power Grids
abstract: The article analyzes various systems for monitoring the condition of high-voltage overhead power transmission lines. The problem of using online monitoring systems for the state of electrical networks is currently relevant. It is known that electric networks with a voltage of 10–500 kV are significantly worn out and it is necessary to improve monitoring systems to prevent the development of possible accidents. Possible causes of failures of overhead power transmission lines are considered. The conducted analysis of accidents in electric networks with a voltage of 10, 110, 500 kV shows that there is a large number of failures of power transmission lines, which could be avoided by implementing systems for monitoring the condition of electric networks. Currently, there is an urgent issue of digitalization of production, a system of integrated digital control over objects distributed over a large area, such as overhead power lines. The introduction of a device for operational monitoring of the technical condition of high-voltage power transmission lines “SMART wire” is considered, the advantages of this device are indicated.

articleTitle: Optimization of Sensor Network's Operation Parameters with Mobile Nodes
abstract: This paper discusses the construction of sensor networks that include highly mobile elements. A brief analysis of modern technologies used in sensor networks is carried out. The difficulties of organizing communication in such networks associated with the need for periodic rebuilding combined with data transmission are indicated. The network organization time durations depending on individual parameters are studied analytically and empirically. The optimal values of these parameters have been found to ensure maximum network performance. The correctness of the choice of these parameters has also been confirmed by tests on specialized simulation software. Recommendations on the application of the solutions found in networks of different sizes are formulated.

articleTitle: Application of Risk-Based Approach to Analyze Damages from Failures of Electrical Equipment
abstract: This article explores the strategy of transitioning from planned maintenance to condition-based maintenance for electric grid facilities, an approach that is becoming increasingly relevant for power grid companies. The focus is on assessing the risks and consequences of equipment failures, which enables the reduction of overhaul costs and enhances the reliability of power grids. Additionally, this approach facilitates more efficient planning of repair activities. The implementation of a risk-oriented strategy requires a comprehensive analysis of the current technical condition of power grids and associated risks to optimize maintenance practices. The article presents a method for managing the electric grid infrastructure, which is based on the principle that risk assessment contributes to improving operational and economic efficiency. Central to this approach is the use of the Technical Condition Index (TCI), which serves as a key factor in risk-oriented maintenance planning.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Patent Image Analysis
abstract: The article describes the novel method for analyzing images of dependency graphs to expand the described physical effects and consists of using deep learning models to determine the types of dependencies of a physical quantity. The software for analyzing patent images has been developed that allows extracting images from patent descriptions in Yandex.Patents and Google Patents. By means of software implementation of the developed algorithm for thematic filtering of patent images (which mainly contain drawings of devices, mathematical and chemical formulas), dataset of dependency graphs of physical quantities is formed. Testing the effectiveness of thematic filtering on a sample based on manually observed images of dependency graphs showed high AUC ROC values of 0.97, accuracy of 0.79. The process of forming a training set of dependency graph images consist 3 stages: a) based on a system request to Google Images; b) using the Matplotlib library to plot graphs of various types of dependencies; c) manually labeled more than 500 images of dependency graphs from patent documents. An algorithm for segmentation of images of dependence graphs has been developed (which allows you to get rid of noisy parts of the image, such as the coordinates of points, their designation, etc.), according to which two cases were tested: (a) using the methods of color spaces, watershed, contour extraction based on the OpenCV library and (b) using the scikit-image library. An algorithm for classifying dependence graphs into 9 classes has been developed using the LSTM, CNN, ViT neural network models.

articleTitle: Improved IMM Algorithm Based on Deep Learning for Maneuvering Target Tracking
abstract: To address the issues of model switching lag and insufficient accuracy in the Interacting Multiple Model (IMM) algorithm for tracking complex maneuvering targets, this paper proposes a deep learning-enhanced improvement method. By designing a deep learning model to generate prior information of model probabilities in real-time and constructing an adaptive fusion mechanism to integrate this information into the IMM framework, the proposed method overcomes the limitations of traditional approaches that rely on fixed transition probability matrices and process noise parameters. Theoretical analysis and application cases demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves model switching speed and state estimation accuracy without significantly increasing computational complexity.

articleTitle: Analysis of Legged Wheels with Spring Suspension for Stair-Climbing Robotics
abstract: The following article looked into legged wheels with spring suspension. The idea behind the work was to see how adding springs in various places and their stiffness would impact the robot's ability to navigate through stairs. Due to the unconventional appearance of legged wheels, they are not suitable for even terrain passage. Hence, the idea was to add springs to minimize shock occurrence each time a leg touches the even environment. It was also important to equip springs throughout the whole path. As the robot progresses through steps, a greater disturbance of the structure occurs. Two different ideas were tested. In the first scenario, springs were attached between the holder of the wheels and the main body. In the second scenario, springs were directly added to the legs. The extruded part of the leg was divided into two, and a spring was embedded between these two parts. Different values of spring stiffness were also examined. The results illustrated that the structure would go further by implementing springs in all four wheels or in the rear. However, the structure was tested only on an upward incline. With other setups, it might be different with the rearrangement of the springs. It was also noted that with higher stiffness of the springs, the structure became unstable. In the second scenario, results illustrated the slightest progress. For instance, when the front wheels' legs were modified, they showed better results. To understand the influence in more depth, further investigation of the problem must be conducted.

articleTitle: Automation of Process of Symbols and Abbreviations Replacement by Words
abstract: Speech synthesisers have requirements for the input text in the Russian language. Numerals, abbreviations, and symbols in text must be transformed into word form in order to ensure the high quality audio output. In this research, the authors, to solve the symbol replacement task, have split it into two natural language processing tasks and have used a different approach for each one. The first task requires the use of regular expressions and the development of algorithms in Python to replace symbols that have a single-word form. The second task requires a more sophisticated approach, as the symbols now have different syntactic forms, which vary by case, gender, and number; therefore, machine learning methods were used, where neural networks were trained using PyTorch, transformers, and public T5-based models. The authors collected sentences with symbols from Wikipedia articles and developed datasets to test the models. The paper shows accuracy, training, and inference time for ruT5-small, ruT5-base-multitask, ruT5-large, fredT5-large models. Also, the authors tested the performance of an ensemble of models to replace symbols and abbreviations.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Problems of Visual Modeling of Internet of Things Components
abstract: The authors study the issues of using visual tools for the system design of complex cyber-physical system components. Based on the analysis of available design tools, effective methods of modeling the components of the Internet of Things have been identified. The main focus is made on the visual analysis of not only design and engineering solutions but also on the resolving of social and manufacturing issues in the development and production of cyber-physical system components. The study examines methods that can significantly improve the efficiency of complex system design. The authors demonstrate the feasibility of integrating visual system design tools with the overall project manufacturing chain, as well as the need for overall synchronization of project procedures during all stages of a systems project.

articleTitle: Reliable Queuing One-Way Delay Metric for Computer Networks
abstract: We claim the method to obtain a reliable queuing one-way delay metric for the wireless computer networking systems. The method requires only a measurement of the timestamp series between packet departure and arrival events. These timestamps are included inside the packets with stream frames. Thus, the method does not need to involve any additional probe packets nor any clock synchronization between two measurement nodes. We describe the algorithm based on the Gerchberg-Saxton procedure for queuing delay decoupling from a measured end-to-end delay distribution. We solve the problem of separating a queuing delay component from the fluctuating transmission and propagation components of delay. The reconstructed queuing delay distribution is further decomposed into individual spectral Weibullian components using the Expectation-Maximization algorithm. We propose an application of temporal queuing delay dynamics to infer a network congestion. Experimental results demonstrate the ability of early congestion detection before packet losses occur.

articleTitle: The Experience of Creating Information Measuring and Control Systems in Metallurgy
abstract: The article discusses two tasks of information systems for monitoring the parameters of technological processes in metalworking creating. In the first task, the width and sickle shape of metal sheets are estimated based on information received from laser rangefinders.
