The task is solved automatically when the flow of metal sheets moves along the roller. The second task is to determine with high accuracy the coordinates of the edge edges of the bent metal sheet in the production of pipes of various diameters. Both tasks are solved automatically using laser rangefinders (profilometers) and original mathematical software. Solving these tasks allows automated quality control of rolled metal products performing and reducing the time spent on the final product. Using of laser profilometers as primary information sources makes it possible to ensure the accuracy required for technological processes. The design of the algorithms assumes low computational complexity, ensuring compliance with time constraints.

articleTitle: On Modeling a Section of Railway Track for the Purpose of Analyzing Changes in the Value of Input Impedance
abstract: The readiness of a railway track for upcoming movement is one of the primary conditions for ensuring the safety of train operations. The systems that currently used in positioning rolling stock either do not allow for the monitoring of the integrity of the rail-wires line or possess high discreetness in determining the location of the rolling stock. In this study, a simulation was conducted to analyze the variation of the input impedance of a railway track section under different conditions. The simulation utilized the Spyder scientific environment, which is an open-source platform for Python. The relationship between the components of the input impedance, the location of the rolling stock, and the insulation resistance of the rail-wires line under specific circumstances is presented. The results obtained from the simulation indicate the possibility of using the value of the complex input impedance to assess the condition of the track section and the location of the rolling stock.

articleTitle: Virtual Voice Assistant for Digital Twin of Production Facility
abstract: The paper considers the use of virtual voice assistants for interaction with industrial facilities and their digital twins. The authors describe the architecture and a set of technologies suitable for the development of voice assistants for production settings. The main focus of this research is the problem of classifying the text of commands obtained by voice recognition in noisy conditions. The authors used fuzzy string matching, string matching with cosine similarity, and machine learning models to recognize commands. Machine learning model was the most reliable command text recognition method of all those reviewed in this paper. The article also presents an example of voice assistant module implementation as part of the software package designed for the development of digital twins of energy facilities.

articleTitle: Methods of Using Artificial Intelligence Algorithms in Human Resource Management
abstract: The study examined the issue of applying artificial intelligence (AI) technologies to job search processes in employment systems. Based on the literature analysis, the main concepts of using AI in human resource management were presented. It was found that in recruitment, there is a relationship between AI replicating human cognitive processes and imitating human learning mechanisms. As a result, 3 main skills for mastering and using AI were presented. The general algorithm and description of the application of AI technologies to the labor market were presented, and the algorithms and methods of the Bat algorithm, the Gaussian distribution approach used in its implementation were studied. A method was proposed in which the optimization process was improved by adding an approach based on the Gaussian distribution to the Bat algorithm. This provides effective training data for vector machines and has been proven to give good results in predicting labor force employment.

articleTitle: Comparison of Time Characteristics of Real-Time Operating Systems (RTOS) on Microcontrollers with Core Architectures ARM and RISC-V
abstract: Real-time operating systems (RTOS) occupy an important place in modern technological processes, becoming an integral part of numerous industries and production cycles. These systems have unique characteristics that allow for effective resource management and ensure a high response speed to external events. This feature is based on the RTOS's ability to redistribute resources between different tasks with varying priorities, guaranteeing the completion of operations within strict time limits. At the same time, microcontrollers, particularly those with cores based on ARM and RISC-V architectures, have become suitable platforms for implementing RTOS due to their compactness and the presence of the necessary hardware conditions. However, despite advancements in technology, RTOS and devices are not without errors and limitations that affect the real-time response to events. This issue has a long history of research for the ARM architecture, as it has become widely used. Microcontrollers with RISC-V cores are gradually emerging and gaining popularity. Developers are adapting RTOS for them. This article aims to investigate the dependence of time-related characteristics, associated with events in RTOS, on the microcontroller core architecture: ARM and RISC-V.

articleTitle: Short-Term Electricity Forecasting of Rolling Shops of Metallurgical Enterprises
abstract: In modern metallurgy, energy efficiency and optimization of electricity use have become critical factors in the competitiveness of manufacturing companies. The increasing energy costs and requirements for environmental compliance encourage companies to implement innovative technologies for energy forecasting and management. Special attention is given to short-term hourly energy consumption forecasts, which help optimize purchases on the wholesale electricity market and reduce costs. The production of hot and cold rolled steel products, which are among the most energy-intensive stages of the metallurgical process, requires effective energy management through accurate forecasting models that consider the specifics of production processes and factors. This article explores machine learning techniques for predicting hourly energy consumption in sheet metal processing one day in advance. The research was conducted by analyzing production data over the past 8 years. Models have been developed and tested based on architectures Random Forest and LSTM, as well as compared them to an existing one-factor regression model. The LSTM model with bidirectional layer showed the best results.

articleTitle: Difficulties of Cluster Analysis on Mixed-Type Variables
abstract: Working with real data often involves clustering of mixed-type variable datasets, which is followed by certain difficulties resulting from lack of guidelines on the usage of clustering methods for mixed-type data. Instead of choosing the optimal method for mixed data clustering, this study aims to determine on which conditions do the specialized cluster analysis methods - hierarchical clustering using Gower's distance and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${k}$</tex>-prototypes algorithm, produce similar partitioning results. Resulting clusterings were after compared with clusters attained by the usage of one-hot encoding technique for transforming categorical data into numerical values. To determine the degree of similarity between methods special metrics were used. Data used in this study is real data obtained from real estate sales advertisements in Saint Petersburg.

articleTitle: Electric Load Forecasting of Railway Enterprises Using the ARIMA Model
abstract: For sustainable operation of railway transport enterprises, taking into account environmental challenges and fluctuations in resource prices, optimizing energy efficiency is becoming a key priority. This includes not only the selection of energy-efficient equipment, but also the use of innovative technologies to reduce energy consumption, as well as forecasting methods. The article discusses the use of the ARIMA model to forecast the electricity consumption of a non-transportation enterprise of JSC Russian Railways. Forecasting was carried out based on hourly electricity consumption data for 1 year. It was found that the discrepancy between the modeled and actual electricity consumption at the facilities of JSC Russian Railways in some cases exceeds 20%. Therefore, the relevance of the study lies in the fact that forecasting using the ARIMA model will improve the efficiency of operational management of electricity consumption processes. The purpose of the study is to forecast the electricity consumption of a non-transportation enterprise of JSC Russian Railways using the ARIMA model. The study found that the ARIMA model is applicable to forecasting electricity consumption in the short term - for 1 day.

articleTitle: Determining the Exact Indoor Location of a Person Using the Channel State Information from the Wi-Fi Router
abstract: The work is devoted to the development of a method for determining the exact location of a person indoor using channel state information received from a Wi-Fi router. The method proposed in this paper is based on processing the phase and amplitude values obtained from the router's service packets by a fully connected neural network. To conduct the experiments, measurements were made with the participation of four people of different genders and physiques, as a result of which more than 500 thousand values of phases and amplitudes were obtained. During the experiments, an accuracy of over 90% was obtained.

articleTitle: Structural Classification of Phase Space Projections with Neural Network-Based Optimization of Sliding Mode Existence Regions for Automated Control System Synthesis
abstract: This paper proposes a method for the structural classification of phase space projections with neural network-based optimization of sliding mode existence regions to facilitate the automated synthesis of control systems based on qualitative analysis of the phase space. Using the Cuk converter as an example, the features of phase space projections in multidimensional systems are studied, along with the limitations inherent to such projections from the perspective of subsequent control law synthesis. A method for circumventing these limitations using sliding mode control is proposed. A technique for generating switching lines for sliding mode control based on phase space projections is introduced, allowing for the classification of projections in terms of their suitability for organizing sliding mode control. Special attention is given to maximizing the area of sliding mode existence regions using a neural network - a multilayer perceptron. It is shown that such neural network-based optimization significantly enhances the potential for selecting control algorithms. The proposed method extends the applicability of phase space projections in the qualitative analysis of multidimensional systems.

articleTitle: Development of an Image Clustering Algorithm for Nanoparticle Extraction
abstract: The article explores the application of the k-means method and its improved versions for clustering nanomaterial images. The purpose of the study is to develop an effective clustering method capable of identifying nanomaterial particles in images with high noise levels. The standard k-means method is compared with its modifications, including as k-means++, MiniBatch k-means, and Elkan, to optimize pixel allocation. The unique properties of these modified methods, including their approaches to assigning pixels to centroids and forming clusters, are examined in detail. Noise reduction filters are described as a preprocessing step to enhance clustering. Practical recommendations for optimizing the clustering process are provided, which can improve accuracy, reliability, and noise resilience. The proposed method is based on clustering techniques that partition images into regions corresponding to the average intensity values within those regions.

articleTitle: Development of a Web Application with a Sheet Movement Visualization System for Tracking the Technological Process in a Sheet Rolling Shop
abstract: The article describes the technology of developing a web application for a sheet rolling shop mnemonic diagram with a sheet metal movement visualization system and an algorithm for processing information flows about their location. The relevance of creating a mnemonic diagram is substantiated. The need to increase transparency in the sheet metal tracking and accounting system through visualization is shown, which is due to the problem of controllability of production processes that lead to downtime on units and corresponding violations in the steel sheet control and accounting system. The web application is a Django application developed using the Redis noSQL DBMS. With the help of the developed algorithm consisting of a sheet movement tracking module and a web interface, developers have the opportunity to debug the application without having to install equipment at the stage of designing and testing the web application. The information flow tracking algorithm, file structure and web page of the application, and the structure of JSON data transmitted to Redis are presented. This approach allows increasing the transparency and efficiency of the 2800 mill, increasing the speed of decision-making on managing production operations in the shop within a shift.

articleTitle: Information Exchange and Adaptive Control in Ant Colonies for Solving Optimization Problems
abstract: The article discusses approaches to improving the ant colony algorithm (ACO) in dynamic and decentralized environments. The main focus is on optimizing the mechanisms of information exchange and adaptive management in the tasks of routing, planning and resource allocation. Three key approaches were identified: local interaction between agents, dynamic parameter tuning, and integration of reinforcement learning based on Q-learning. Each of the approaches was analyzed in terms of efficiency, computational costs, and adaptability to tasks with changing conditions. As part of the experiments conducted on the basis of a five-node network, a small-scale assessment was carried out. The results showed that for networks with moderate dynamics and an average number of nodes, the optimal approach is local interaction, minimizing computational costs and speeding up adaptation. In conditions of high environmental variability, dynamic parameter setting provides a more flexible and adaptive solution. For tasks where it is important to take into account experience and predict future conditions, the Q-learning approach is most effective.

articleTitle: Analysis of Oscillations in Nonlinear Human-Operated Robotic System
abstract: The development of automation is characterized by the increasing complexity of control tasks associated with various technical objects. However, this does not exclude the human element from the control process. Manual control has certain drawbacks that negatively impact the quality of management, primarily arising from the interaction between the operator and the nonlinear dynamics of the robot. This study examines a manual control system for a robotic manipulator, taking into account nonlinear constraints that may manifest as limitations on the power of the actuating mechanism or as part of a local regulator. The parameters of the operator's control actions exhibit a certain range due to individual characteristics of the human operator or the control technique employed. Additionally, signal transmission delays may be present in the control loop. Considering these system characteristics provides a more comprehensive understanding of control quality and allows for the establishment of acceptable control techniques for the human operator. Depending on the frequency of input disturbances, this work analyzes the closed-loop system comprising the operator and manipulator using methods based on harmonic linearization of nonlinearity and harmonic balance equations: locus of a perturbed relay system and harmonic stabilization. The results of calculations and simulations using these methods indicate that there exists a parameter space within which oscillations may arise. Thus, when designing manual control systems for robotic manipulators, it is essential to pay attention to the control techniques employed by the human operator and to overall delays in order to avoid undesirable operational modes of the system.

articleTitle: Integration of Large Language Models and Computer Vision Algorithms in LMS: A Methodology for Automated Verification of Software Tasks and Multimodal Analysis of Educational Data
abstract: This paper presents a study on the design and development of a learning management system (LMS) integrated with large language models (LLMs) and image recognition/generation algorithms to automate software task validation and multimodal educational data analysis. The purpose of the development is to improve the quality of feedback for learners, deepen the understanding of errors made and expand the capabilities of the system by synthesizing formal LLM models and visual processing algorithms. The system is based on the use of domestic LLMs such as GigaChat and YandexGPT, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) technology, and modern computer vision algorithms. The system architecture is described, including GitVerse for code storage, GitVerse Actions for automated testing of solutions in Docker containers, and image processing modules for analyzing and generating visual data in the educational process. The conducted experiment demonstrates the effectiveness of the integrative approach, which allows to improve the quality of feedback and increase the performance of students. Prospects for further research include optimization of computational resources and development of techniques for integrated analysis of multimodal educational data.

articleTitle: Organization of a Digital Twin System Based on the Subsystem of Vibration Diagnostics of Cutting Processes in Metal Cutting Machines Using MEMS Measurement Technology
abstract: The article discusses issues related to the formation of the structure of the vibration diagnostics system, which could serve as a measuring subsystem for the digital twin of machining processes on metal-cutting machines. The article proposes the basis of this system, consisting of vibration sensors based on MEMS, as well as possible schemes for implementing such a system in the context of metal turning on metal-cutting machines with a revolver head. In terms of the software content of the digital twin system, the issue of neural network search for parameters of virtual models of the digital twin is being considered. Based on this approach, parametric identification of mathematical models is carried out, which are used to evaluate the current output values of the vibration monitoring system and the calculated (target) values of the quality indicators of the cutting process.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Diabetes Mellitus Based on Artificial Intelligence Algorithms
abstract: It is known that artificial intelligence algorithms provide inference capabilities about new objects based on the analysis of an existing dataset. This feature of artificial intelligence makes it possible to use it as a solution in many issues. One such problem is the issue of diagnosing diabetes mellitus, which is considered one of the most common diseases in medicine. This research work is devoted to the solution of this issue, the study highlights the process of diagnosing diabetes mellitus based on classification algorithms. In the study, the data set is selected first and this data set is passed through the data profling and data cleaning stages. Based on the compiled data set, the artificial intelligence algorithms Logistic regression, Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forest, and Nearest Neighbors are taught and tested. In order to increase the accuracy of the results of the study, the hyper parameters of the selected artificial intelligence model are adjusted. The results obtained after the study are analyzed and the research conclusion is made.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Driven Web System for Automated Sequential-to-Parallel Code Transformation
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a machine learning-driven web system for automating the transformation of sequential code into parallel code. The proposed system leverages a shared memory programming model and is built on a microservices architecture to ensure scalability and modularity. It incorporates advanced tools for constructing and analyzing Abstract Syntax Trees to generate parallel programs that adhere to Bernstein's conditions. A supervised learning mechanism, using Word2Vec for vector representation and TF-IDF for significance evaluation, enables the system to adapt and refine parallelization rules based on programmer input. Additionally, the system integrates an AMQP-based message broker to handle high-load processing efficiently and supports data storage through relational or NoSQL databases. The solution provides a robust and flexible platform for enhancing computational performance and reducing development complexity in parallel programming. The results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach in addressing the challenges of automating code parallelization in modern software systems.

articleTitle: A Technique for Protecting Machine Learning Components of Intrusion Detection Systems from Evasion Attacks
abstract: Today, intrusion detection systems (IDS) are important means to protect network infrastructure from cyber attacks. Digitalisation requires the use of tools that can cope not only with known types of attacks, but also with previously unspecified ones. Machine learning (ML) can be used to defend against such threats. This paper presents a methodology for defending against evasion attacks on machine learning (ML) components of intrusion detection systems. For the first time, Long short-term memory (LSTM) defence modelling against Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM) was performed for IDS ML components. Precision, Recall, and F-measure metrics were used for evaluation. The study shows the possibility of protecting IDS ML components from evasion attacks and provides an effective technique for such protection.

articleTitle: Instant Road Marking Line Segmentation Method for Highly Automated Vehicles
abstract: The paper deals with methods and means of detecting road marking lines in images obtained from cameras of highly automated vehicles (HAVS). The proposed method is based on a two-stage detection process, in which first the lines are segmented (Instance Segmentation), and then parameterized models of the lines are determined using the neural network model YOLOv8n-seg, which can be further used in algorithms of autonomous driving. Such a process allows efficient identification and localization of road marking lines in complex road conditions. In this paper, the first stage of road marking line detection, i.e., intrinsic segmentation, is considered. Test results of the proposed approach are presented, including an evaluation of its performance and accuracy on different test datasets.

articleTitle: Control of Continuous Polymer Synthesis Processes Using Heuristic Optimization Methods
abstract: This paper addresses the development of efficient methods for controlling polymer synthesis processes using heuristic optimization techniques. To solve the problem of determining optimal conditions for complex chemical-technological processes, a genetic algorithm is proposed. The key stages of its implementation are defined using modern software development tools. A kinetic modeling approach is presented for evaluating the primary molecular characteristics of polymer products, based on the use of statistical moments of the molecular weight distribution. The application of the genetic algorithm to this process enabled the identification of an optimal two-point control regime, facilitating the production of polymers with desired properties. Computational experiments demonstrated that variations in the mode of regulator feed in conditions of multi-point molecular weight control constitute a significant factor in managing complex processes. This approach provides a basis for planning the molecular parameters of polymer products in the context of continuous production systems.

articleTitle: Software System for Biometric Human Authentication Based on Handwritten Signature Dynamics
abstract: In this work, we present a software system for biometric authentication based on the dynamics of handwritten signatures. Our proposed approach focuses on analyzing dynamic signature characteristics, such as pen tip coordinates, pressure, azimuth, and tilt, captured using a graphics tablet. We employed normalization and interpolation techniques for time series data processing and feature extraction. A key feature of our developed method is the application of fuzzy set theory to model complex and subjective features like pressure patterns and writing rhythm. This allows for consideration of individual handwriting characteristics and improves authentication accuracy. The system analyzes a wide range of characteristics, including signature length, relative proportions (height-to-width ratio), average pressure, relative pen-up duration, pressure unevenness, and the area enclosed by the time series graph. The developed system was experimentally tested on the MCYT_Signature_100 database. The results demonstrate the high effectiveness of the proposed method, especially with limited training data. The proposed solution can be integrated into various security systems and applied in areas such as banking, electronic voting, access control systems, and document authorship verification.

articleTitle: Analysis of the “Extended Kalman Filter – Adaptive Digital Filter” System Operation in Filtering of Non-Stationary Signals
abstract: Processing of various origin non-stationary signals in control systems for robotic devices is an urgent problem. The use of the extended Kalman filter (EKF) for working with non-stationary signals, including signal filtering, is limited by the precise settings of the filter — the observed system model and the covariance matrices of the EKF algorithm, which requires the adaptability of the filter algorithm under conditions of an input rapidly changing noised non-stationary signal. In this regard, the paper proposes to use the system “extended Kalman filter — adaptive digital filter” (EKF-ADF system) for filtering of non-stationary signals, which is the EKF augmented with an adaptive digital filter with the NLMS (normalized least mean squares) adaptation algorithm in order to compensate for the error in the operation of the EKF when non-stationary signal filtering is performing. The study of the operation of the EKF-ADF system as a filter for non-stationary signals shows that under conditions of a significant noise applied on a non-stationary signal, the algorithm of the EKF-ADF system, in comparison with the EKF algorithm, which has settings similar to the EKF settings in the EKF-ADF system, possesses the highest values of the “signal-to-noise ratio” evaluation of filtering results. The EKF-ADF system can be used as a state observer of robotic devices, which is capable of operating under conditions of non-stationary processes.

articleTitle: Digital Twin-Based Module for the Analysis of the Mechanical Response of Crystalline Materials
abstract: This paper presents the development of a digital module designed for the storage and analysis of mechanical response characteristics in crystalline materials. The module processes the stiffness tensor obtained from structural models derived through quantum-chemical methods, incorporating periodic boundary conditions. It includes comprehensive data on the mechanical properties of organic crystalline compounds, highlighting significant features such as elastic moduli, directions of maximum and minimum compressibility, and negative linear compressibility. The collected data undergoes thorough processing and analysis, focusing on the distribution of critical elastic modulus values. This dataset is prepared for future processing using artificial intelligence techniques, enabling the construction of predictive models and enhancing the exploration of “structure-property” relationships. Additionally, an algorithm for visualizing spatial dependencies of Young's modulus, linear compressibility, linear stiffness, and uniaxial compressibility has been implemented, allowing for adjustable resolution. This visualization is integrated with atomic-molecular systems, including periodic structures, to elucidate the relationship between mechanical response and crystal structure. A user-friendly interface has also been developed for loading and storing raw data, facilitating the analysis of mechanical response characteristics derived from quantum-chemical calculations. Configuration files for the web server container have been created to support continuous software integration and deployment on new platforms. This innovative digital module represents a significant advancement in the field of materials science, contributing to improved understanding and optimization of crystalline materials for various applications.

articleTitle: Calculating Singular Integrals with Cauchy Kernels in Digital Processing of Gastroenterological Medical Signals
abstract: This article within the framework of the research work is devoted to the study of the problem of integrals. Singular integrals are usually encountered in the deep analysis of biomedical signals, which are characterized by sharp changes in continuity and discontinuity. Efficient and accurate evaluation of this type of integral is of great importance in the diagnostic process, especially in spectral analysis and identification of specific signals in gastrointestinal diseases. In this article, I have extensively discussed the mathematical foundations of the use of Cauchy kernels for the approximate calculation of singular integrals and their algorithmic methods. In this regard, modern methods are proposed to further improve the accuracy of signal detection, noise suppression and accuracy in the diagnostic process, since the complexity of gastrointestinal signals and the negative impact of noise and interference on performance are also considered in this study. The proposed method simplifies the interpretation of complex signals, increases the accuracy of spectral analysis results, and automates medical procedures. These methods, in addition to increasing diagnostic accuracy, create new ways to correctly assess the patient's condition using medical markers. The relevance of the research to the development of algorithmic solutions adapted to data processing and biomedical interpretation processes increases its relevance. Therefore, the application of modern technology in medicine largely depends on this research.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Methods for Multimodal Classification of Personality Traits Using Social Media Data
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the effectiveness of various machine learning methods for the multimodal classification of personality traits using the HEXACO model and open data from social media users. Particular attention is paid to the analysis of data obtained from user profiles, including statistical, visual, and audio characteristics. For each personality trait from the HEXACO model, a machine learning model is trained that determines the manifestation degree of this trait (low, medium, high). The influence of different types of information, both individually and in combination, on the weighted F1-score is considered. The study provides a comparative analysis of traditional machine learning methods that use all features and approaches with the selection of the most significant features. A strategy for combining data from different modalities using early merger is evaluated. The experimental results demonstrate that early merger models using selected features from different modalities provide the best result of the weighted F1-score, which varies depending on the personality trait from 0.76 to 0.85.

articleTitle: Research on the Effectiveness of Enhanced Control Algorithms for the Electrical Modes of a Ladle Furnace Installation
abstract: In this article, issues related to improving the energy efficiency of ladle-furnace installations (LFs) through the development and implementation of advanced control algorithms for electrical modes are considered. The main focus is on reducing the specific energy consumption <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(W_{spec})$</tex>, which is one of the key factors in enhancing the economic efficiency of steelmaking production. Within this research, a comprehensive analysis of the existing operating modes of LFs was conducted, during which reserves for optimizing the heating processes of liquid steel and improving the thermal efficiency of electric arcs were identified. Additionally, new algorithms for automatic switching of working curves and stages of the furnace transformer's OLTP (tap change under load) were developed, based on the analysis of the harmonic composition of the arc currents. These algorithms enable dynamic adaptation of the electrical modes of LFs to changing conditions of argon blowing and slag regimes, ensuring minimization of thermal losses and electricity consumption reduction. The obtained results demonstrate the significance of applying modern methods of controlling electrical modes to enhance the energy efficiency and competitiveness of steelmaking processes.

articleTitle: One-Shot Visual Detection of Phishing Resources with CLIP ViT and Contrastive Learning
abstract: We propose a method for detecting phishing sites based on analyzing visual similarity with trusted web pages. The developed original approach utilizes the CLIP ViT model trained on its own dataset using triplet loss to generate page embeddings in a compact vector space. The key feature is the introduction of a multimodal representation of embeddings and the use of one-shot classification to detect new phishing resources without the need to retrain the model. The proposed approach combines visual and textual representation of web pages to improve robustness against HTML code and URL changes. A combined learning strategy including batch-hard triplet loss with soft margin and embedding regularization through MSE minimization between image and text representations is introduced. A series of experiments are conducted on a large set of real web pages containing legitimate and phishing sites. The obtained results demonstrate the high accuracy of the method, surpassing traditional approaches in terms of robustness to page modifications. The possibility of integrating the proposed system into the infrastructure of automated web threat monitoring is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Designing a Power System Digital Twin as a Core of the Domain-Aware Digital Platform
abstract: The paper presents an approach to designing a digital twin as a core of the domain-aware digital platform. Methodological aspects of digital transformation and platform design are discussed. The model-based digital twin architecture and development process are elaborated. To formalize and automate this process, we propose to apply novel mathematical methods based on category theory, such as a flexible multicomma construction. The generic distribution of the digital twin models across components of the platform and applications is presented. We illustrate our approach with examples from the electric power energy sector, where energy management platforms emerge while the power system digital twin technology is gradually overcoming the difficulties associated with design and deployment.

articleTitle: Secure Routing Protocol Based on FANET
abstract: The flying ad-hoc network (FANET) technology-based secure routing protocol described in this study functions between a ground station and a UAV network. This protocol employs a hybrid authentication technique to guarantee communication dependability. The system is based on an asymmetric method that ensures secure connections between the UAV and the ground control station, as well as between the UAVs themselves. A symmetric scheme with digital signatures is used to encrypt the routing. Before joining the network, the UAV must register. During the registration process, the Key Distribution Center provides the necessary public and private keys for each node that wants to connect. Furthermore, crucial routing data is safeguarded using the TWINE algorithm. Wormhole attacks are avoided by using the packet binding method. Even in the event of an aggressor attack, simulations show that this routing system can sustain effective network functioning, ensuring a high packet delivery ratio and optimal network costs.

articleTitle: OSINT Model of Privacy Violator
abstract: The emergence of publicly available OSINT (Open Source Intelligence) tools often leads to leaks of confidential information and the collection of data for conducting cyberattacks. At the same time, open publications lack a model of an intruder using OSINT, which prevents the development of a theory to counter OSINT. The aim of the article is to develop a model of a confidentiality intruder utilizing OSINT. Methods. The OSINT intruder model is constructed by applying the theory of algebraic morphisms to information security problems. Results. A model of an OSINT intruder has been developed, formalizing the relationship between open and confidential properties of an object and their mutual mapping. A task to be solved by an OSINT intruder is defined, and attack vectors are described. A hypothesis regarding the necessary and sufficient conditions for successfully breaching confidentiality using OSINT is proposed. Discussion. The existence of an inverse mapping of confidential properties to open ones requires further study.

articleTitle: Analysis of Associative and Sentimental Characteristics of Words for Revealing Hidden Emotions and Correlations
abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between text sentiment and associations, using data from open lexicographic resources: the Associative Dictionary and the Sentiment Dictionary of the Russian Language “KartaSlovSent”. The aim of the study is to explore how associative links can complement traditional sentiment analysis methods, uncover hidden emotional nuances, and refine the contextual interpretation of text. The paper proposes a data processing algorithm that includes stages of loading, merging, aggregating, and analyzing the distribution of sentiment associations. The results show that associative links can expand the sentiment lexicon, account for the context in which words are used, and identify local anomalies in emotional perception. A positive correlation was found between the numerical sentiment score of words and the share of positive associations. However, the study also revealed that the prevalence of neutral associations may reduce the accuracy of the analysis. Thus, the use of associations in sentiment analysis tasks is an effective auxiliary tool that can significantly improve the quality of emotional tone evaluation when integrated with traditional methods and machine learning models.

articleTitle: Adaptive Simulated Binary Crossover with Bayesian Optimization for Industrial Applications
abstract: Genetic Algorithms are widely used as global optimization solvers for complex and non-convex problems in industrial applications (resource and load planning, workshop logistics, process control, etc.). Simulated Binary Crossover (SBX) is a common operator in real-coded Genetic Algorithms for continuous optimization, but it typically relies on a fixed distribution index parameter that may not stay optimal throughout the evolutionary process. To address this, we propose a Transfer Learning-Based Adaptive Simulated Binary Crossover approach, which employs Bayesian Optimization to dynamically update the parameter during the Genetic Algorithm run. The parameter is periodically re-optimized based on the population's current dynamics. Tested on benchmark functions including Rosenbrock, Rastrigin, Ackley, and Griewank, our method achieves faster convergence and higher solution quality than standard Genetic Algorithms with a fixed parameter.

articleTitle: Price Optimization Method for Highly Technological Products
abstract: We examined the pricing model of high-tech products according to several management criteria: revenue and profit. It is shown that optimal solutions are significantly different. The research method uses the elasticity of demand and the elasticity of profit. A model of a rational price using an essential factor is given: maximum profitability and marginal profit. The analytical processing of large data sets allows information collection to identify model parameters. The actual data on marginal profit and variable costs for various companies in the “22.11 Manufacture of Rubber Tires” industry are considered. Examples of calculating the optimal price by specified parameters for a particular company are considered.

articleTitle: Development of an Algorithm for Intelligent Analysis of Data From a Microprocessor-Based Portable Spectrophotometer
abstract: This article is devoted to the development of a microprocessor-based portable spectrophotometer for the analysis of substances in water, the development of an algorithm for analyzing data from the device, and the writing of software based on this algorithm. In addition, the article is devoted to assessing the applicability and relevance of this device for high-quality water monitoring. The article presents a structural diagram and an optical system diagram of a microprocessor-based portable spectrophotometer. In addition to the microcontroller, the portable device also uses at least two logical modules: a servo drive and a Bluetooth module. The principle of operation of the device's microcontroller is presented in the form of a structural diagram, the entire developed algorithm is divided into two main stages - a preparatory cycle and the main cycle in which samples are studied. A special algorithm has been developed that allows remote control of the spectrophotometer. In addition, the algorithm for intelligent data analysis has several operating modes and a calibration mode.

articleTitle: Development of a Statistical Analyzer to Identify Malicious Code in Information Systems
abstract: Currently, the search for malicious code in information systems is relevant. The analysis showed that existing static analyzers detect vulnerabilities in the code, but not malicious code, as a result of which it was decided to create a new static analyzer with zero false positives, which will not only search for malicious code, but also indicate its location. A formalized representation of the task of detecting malicious code based on static analysis using set theory based on the introduction of a function that matches each element with a maliciousness factor is proposed. A technique for detecting malicious code in the source code based on lexical, semantic and static analysis has been developed. An experimental study has shown that the accuracy of detecting malicious code has increased by three percent, and the F1 measure - by five percent, compared to the best similar tool, which indicates a more effective performance of the task of detecting malicious code by the developed algorithm compared to analogs.

articleTitle: Dynamic Algorithm for Load Distribution Between Computing Resources of Cloud Environments
abstract: The article considers the development of a dynamic algorithm for distributing and balancing the load, characterized by nonlinear parameters and fractal structure, between the computing resources of cloud data centers (DCs). A rationale is given for the application of methods of nonlinear dynamics and chaos theory to solving this problem, which is based on the topological similarity of the behavior of deterministic chaotic systems and the input network load of the data center. The load randomness test was conducted by calculating Lyapunov indices. To eliminate noise components of network traffic, the principal component method of its time series was applied. The problem of phase space reconstruction is solved by the delay method based on the embedding theorem and the average mutual information method. Based on this reconstruction, a method for predicting the load dynamics was developed. It was presented in the form of a system of discrete mappings connected by an algebraic polynomial, providing successful prediction of irregular time series and forming the basis for constructing a matrix for distributing data center resources. The aim of the article is to increase the efficiency of using the resources of data center cluster servers in conditions of a fractal structure of the network load by developing a dynamic algorithm for its distribution and balancing based on nonlinear dynamics methods.

articleTitle: Risk Management Issues for Managing Information Security Solutions
abstract: The article proposes an approach with which it is possible to analyze the impact of information security on the decision management process. Using this approach in the system life cycle reduces risks and helps identify bottlenecks, including in the field of information security. The efficiency of the approach is shown on examples. Also risks, associated with objective and subjective factors are considered, and an example of integral risk their calculation is given in the article. A set of actions to assess the risk of reliability violations is presented. The structure of the modeled system is shown without taking into consideration the information security requirements. The probability of reliability violation of the implementation of the decision management process for different process elements, as well as the importance of the risk of violation of the reliability implementation of the decision management process, are determined.

articleTitle: Assessing the Knowledge of Students in the Field of Computer Networks Using Associative Experiments
abstract: The presented study compares the freeform and directed types of linguistic associative experiments. The objective of these experiments was twofold: firstly, to evaluate the effectiveness of each method in analyzing the level of students' knowledge in a particular subject area, and secondly, to gain insight into their knowledge model. The analysis of the results showed that the directed experiment allows obtaining more accurate reactions characterizing the student's knowledge of the chosen subject area. It is better suited to work with students of profile directions, but requires more resources for conducting and processing the data. The freeform experiment, on the contrary, is less labor-intensive and allows obtaining a wide range of associations reflecting a general picture of students' knowledge. However, its results may not be as structured and require additional interpretation. Both methods have advantages and disadvantages. The choice between them should be based on specific research objectives and available resources. The introduction of modern information and communication technologies, including neural networks, artificial intelligence and machine learning, can greatly simplify data processing and speed up the process of building an infocognitive knowledge model from the collected data.

articleTitle: The Simulation Model of Multipath Data Transmission in Wireless Networks with Interference
abstract: Load balancing methods in networks aim to distribute traffic evenly between nodes to prevent overloading of individual routes and improve overall network performance. For instance, machine learning-based routing allows you to analyze network behavior and predict optimal routes for data transmission, which is especially effective in complex dynamic networks. Another option is Pareto Optimization, which is used to consider multiple criteria, such as minimizing latency and energy consumption, simultaneously. The reliability of networks, especially wireless ones, is becoming an issue that requires solutions that can adapt to constantly changing conditions, creating stable communication systems. The article describes and tests a simulation model of a wireless network in which requests are sent from sources through towers to two different recipients simultaneously along several paths. The use of intermediate switching nodes allows using the AOMDV protocol to build different data transmission routes. The simulation results for various modifications of the model allow us to evaluate the advantages of using multipath routing.

articleTitle: Formation of a Digital Twin of the Customer of Digital Transport Platform Services
abstract: High competition in the organization of supply chains has led to a fierce struggle for the customer. In this situation, customers of logistics services tend to give preference to companies that are able to meet the most demanding requirements for the quality of supply chain organization. In this regard, carrier companies seeking to strengthen their position in the market are actively studying their customers, studying their needs in detail in order to satisfy them as fully as possible. In modern conditions, this data can be used to create a digital twin of the customer, which is a virtual model that allows predicting customer behavior. For this purpose, this study was conducted to collect and analyze customer feedback data on a digital transport platform. The analysis showed customer preferences characterizing the quality of supply chains.

articleTitle: Development and Analysis of Algorithms for Measuring of Communication Links Parameters in Internet of Things Software Defined Networks
abstract: The article considers methods for measuring parameters of communication links connecting OpenFlow switches in software defined networks of the Internet of Things to ensure the operation of dynamic routing algorithms. Theoretical information on the parameters of communication links that ensure quality of service in the network and methods for measuring them using a network controller are given. Step-by-step algorithms for implementing measurement of delay, packet loss percentage, bandwidth and load of communication links using the Ryu controller are given. Experimental studies confirming the operability of the presented algorithms are conducted. A comparison of the proposed algorithms with the operation of other utilities for measuring communication links parameters, such as Ping and Iperf3, is carried out. It is shown that the quality of the proposed algorithms for measuring delay and packet loss percentage using the controller show similar results to the quality of the Ping and Iperf3 utilities. The limitations imposed on the operation of the presented algorithm for measuring the bandwidth of communication links are shown. This study is an integral part of the project on developing intelligent algorithms for dynamic routing in software defined networks.

articleTitle: Adversarial Attack on YOLO Neural Network
abstract: This paper describes and demonstrates a comprehensive analysis of structured criteria of formalized conditions for creating universal images falsely classified by computer vision algorithms called adversarial examples based on YOLO neural network models. In this paper, a pattern was identified and studied using the above mathematical model of the proposed algorithm for the successful creation of a universal destructive image depending on the generated dataset, on which neural networks were trained using a fast sign gradient attack. This pattern is demonstrated for YOLO 8, YOLO 9, YOLO 10, and YOLO 11 classifier models trained on the basis of the standard COCO dataset.

articleTitle: Big Data Collection and Analysis in Warehouse Management
abstract: This article explores the use of big data technologies to enhance warehouse management efficiency. The primary focus is on analyzing data collection, processing, and visualization methods and their role in process automation and decision-making. Methods of big data collection, machine learning algorithms for demand forecasting and inventory optimization are presented. The research findings indicate that the application of analytical technologies contributes to cost reduction, improved inventory accuracy, and faster order processing. Special attention is given to demand modeling based on historical data and external factors, such as weather conditions and market trends. The article discusses the advantages and limitations of various approaches, including ARIMA, SARIMA, XGBoost, and neural networks, for inventory management. Thus, the study highlights the importance of integrating big data into warehouse logistics to achieve high performance and adaptability.

articleTitle: Development of RL DDPG Agent for Planning Energy-Efficient Trajectory of Collaborative Robot
abstract: In the global scientific community, there are already approaches to optimizing robot trajectories based on classical mathematical methods. These methods often require significant computational resources, especially when solving high-dimensional problems in real time. In this regard, the use of approximate solutions, such as neural networks and reinforcement learning methods, is becoming a promising direction. In this paper, we train the Reinforcement Learning Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient method for creating an agent for optimizing robot trajectories based on the energy consumption criterion. The agent demonstrated the ability to plan trajectories with minimal energy consumption, with an error of no more than 1.3%. This proves the effectiveness of the trained method and its applicability in real production conditions.

articleTitle: Application of Integral Values in Relay Protection and Emergency Automation Devices Based on Arduino
abstract: Relay protection and emergency automation systems serve as automatic safeguards against damage and abnormal operating conditions in electrical components of power grids. They constitute a critical component that ensures the reliability and stability of these systems. The increasing demands on power systems, including higher loads, longer transmission lines, and stringent requirements for stability, pose challenges to the functioning of relay protection systems. Simultaneously, there is an increasing expectation for their operational efficiency. Consequently, there is a constant evolution in relay protection technology, with the goal of developing more advanced devices that align with the demands of the contemporary electricity industry. The majority of accidents in power systems are attributed to the operation of microprocessor-based relay protection devices that rely on similar physical principles. Additionally, one of the contributing factors to these incidents is the saturation of current transformers during short circuits, leading to a cascading effect in the network. This scenario becomes particularly critical when the malfunctioning of the protection system is a result of current transformer saturation. Such failures can result in the complete separation of the power grid, necessitating independent operation. Notable examples include incidents at the Rostov and Kalinin nuclear power plants. In response to this challenge, a novel microprocessor-based device will be designed and developed. Unlike existing solutions, this device will utilize integral measurements to provide a comprehensive analysis.

articleTitle: Analysis of Functional Parameters of Fiber-Optic Sensors Based on Mandelstam-Brillouin Scattering Principle
abstract: In recent twenty years fiber optic sensors using Mandelstam Brillouin scattering effect have obtained a wide application in distributed measurements of temperature and deformation. Their application in engineering structures requires the analysis of functional parameters under conditions of noise interference onto backscatter signal spectrum. The research presents a mathematical model for measurement process based on stimulated scattering emphasizing on the measurement errors analysis. The formulas are presented for evaluation of mean quadratic errors in temperature and deformation measurements depending on noise-to-signal ratio and number of measurement cycles. In addition, methods to assess spatial resolution and dynamic range are proposed. Variations in methods for detection and processing backscattering spectra make it possible to produce efficient sensor systems which can monitor parameter change in real time.

articleTitle: Automation of Visualization of Indicators of Product Quality Assessment at an Industrial Enterprise
abstract: The article considers the problem of developing a solution for automating the process of visualizing indicators of the quality assessment of manufactured products at an industrial enterprise. The existing methods and tools for data visualization are considered, the architecture and main components of the proposed automation system are presented, and the advantages of the proposed solution compared to traditional approaches are discussed. A description of the process of creating a computer program designed to automate the processing of big data and their visualization is proposed. The structured data entering the program are metal quality indicators, which are obtained on the basis of processing reporting documentation from the enterprise information system. The features of software libraries and methods of working with them are described, and an algorithm for the software module is developed. Data visualization in the form of graphs is based on information about faulty products, presented as multidimensional data.

articleTitle: Developing AI Models Using a Code-Free Platform
abstract: This paper examines the evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) technology and its impact on the development of intelligent products. With the advancements in machine learning and AI, the developer community has provided various frameworks and Python libraries, such as PyTorch and TensorFlow, to support the development of intelligent products. These tools have simplified the development process, but constructing intelligent systems remains challenging for non-specialists. Consequently, no-code intelligent development platforms have emerged, which lower the barrier to entry through visual interaction interfaces. The article also discusses the development process of intelligent agents, particularly the challenges associated with large language models, including computational requirements, costs, and expertise. Finally, the article demonstrates the process and advantages of developing intelligent agents through a no-code approach using the TWIN24AI platform as a case study.

articleTitle: Information Security Management by Optimizing the Security Toolkit with Game Theory
abstract: The paper examines the issue of managing the information security system by selecting and forming an optimal set of means of protecting the information technology object. To solve this problem, it is proposed to use game theory algorithms, the payment matrices of which are reduced to modeling conflict situations and choosing optimal strategies based on the Bayes, Wald, Hurwitz and Laplace criteria. An example of applying these criteria to select strategies is given. The example is based on the results of analyzing statistical material on current cyber threats and the probabilities of their reflection by various means of protecting the information technology object. Experimental evaluation has shown that the proposed approach allows for ensuring the required level of information security.

articleTitle: The Approach to Recognition of Process Data Metering Devices Using Their Digital Fingerprints
abstract: The paper examines the problem of assessing the correctness of data from metering devices in technological systems. To solve this problem, it is proposed to identify a device by its digital fingerprint, based on its signal's dynamic model. The procedure for creating a digital fingerprint and the approach to comparing the reference digital fingerprint with the current one to detect the fact of substitution of the device or its signal are presented. The basic requirements for the input data used to create a digital fingerprint have been formulated. The criteria for selecting dynamic signal models suitable for use in the metering device recognition procedure are formulated. The application of the proposed procedure is considered using industrial temperature and humidity sensors as an example.

articleTitle: Using Incomplete Clustering Models for Big Data Analysis
abstract: The use of Big Data in the generation of solutions has become an important part of modern engineering and management processes. Big data is a collection of information that is too large or complex to be processed by traditional methods. This data can be structured or unstructured. Big data and Zwicky morphological analysis are powerful tools for generating and analyzing engineering solutions (ES). Also, the use of two approaches makes it possible to adapt the analysis process to the dynamic and complex conditions of modern technologies. Incomplete clustering is proposed, in which only a part of the solutions is grouped into clusters. In the context of synthesizing and analyzing multiple ES, incomplete clustering helps manage uncertainty and variety of possible solutions without forcing each solution to be tied to a specific group. Incomplete clustering is useful for dividing multiple engineering solutions into groups based on key characteristics. Also, the proposed approach, taking into account incomplete information, helps to more accurately account for risks and reduce the likelihood of making bad decisions.

articleTitle: Quantum Neural Networks: Bridging Topological Structures and Variational Quantum Circuits
abstract: This paper presents the concept of quantum neural networks (QNN), a new framework that combines quantum computing with topological data analysis to process data defined on simplicial complexes. Based on the fundamentals of topological signal processing and variational quantum circuits, QNN aim to use the structure of simplicial complexes to perform efficient calculations and extract higher-order relational patterns from data. The proposed architecture uses quantum layers (QL), which map interactions between simplices into quantum circuits, providing both in-order and inter-order interactions. The paper describes two QL variants: basic and schematic, providing flexibility for applications with varying complexity. In addition, the paper explores the theoretical foundations of simplicial complexes, quantum neural networks, and the interaction between classical and quantum approaches in data encoding, state evolution and optimization. By leveraging quantum algorithms and eliminating current hardware limitations, QNN promise scalability and enhanced performance for applications in optimization, numerical simulation, and complex systems modeling. This research demonstrates the potential of QNN to advance the field of quantum machine learning, paving the way for future developments of quantum algorithms and their practical applications.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in a Modern Information and Computing Complex for Managing the Operating Modes of Power Supply Systems
abstract: At present, information technology systems are increasingly being developed, resulting in the need for more efficient interaction and data processing. Modern data volumes are becoming so large that a person is not always able to effectively cope with the task at hand. This leads to the need to create and use automated systems that can reduce the workload on a person. One of such systems is the information and computing complex “Gorizont ”. To ensure more efficient interaction in the Horizon IVC, it is proposed to implement a virtual assistant based on artificial intelligence since it can significantly increase the efficiency of the system, providing fast data processing, automation of routine tasks and simplification of interaction with users. This will reduce the workload of personnel, minimize errors and increase overall productivity. The virtual assistant will be able to analyze data, predict events and make decisions, making the Gorizont system a more flexible and adaptive program. Further development of the idea of introducing artificial intelligence will allow data exchange between certified systems of JSC Russian Railways and the system operator: OIC Dispatcher of JSC SO UES, IVK Gorizont, ARM of the Energy Dispatcher of JSC Russian Railways, ARM of the train dispatcher of JSC Russian Railways. Such unification of systems will allow to optimize the operating modes of external and traction power supply systems leading to more rational consumption of electrical energy.

articleTitle: Model and Algorithm for Data Distribution in the Microservice Architecture of a Web Application
abstract: This paper is devoted to the study and development of a model and algorithm for data distribution in the microservice architecture of a web application, considering the possible inoperability of some services. The research focuses on enhancing the performance of load balancers by considering key parameters such as request intensity, system capacity, and reliability. A mathematical model is formulated using queuing theory and Erlang's formulas to define the optimal function for data distribution. The study proposes an improved algorithm for dynamic load balancing that actively monitors microservice performance, reducing bottlenecks and increasing processing efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate a significant improvement in the output flow of serviced data messages, increasing throughput by 15.25% compared to conventional load balancing methods. The proposed approach enables efficient utilization of system resources, enhances fault tolerance, and improves request execution speeds in microservice-based web applications. These findings highlight the importance of adaptive data distribution mechanisms in high-load environments, ensuring reliability and scalability for modern banking and financial services applications.

articleTitle: Improving Energy Efficiency of 5000 Plate Mill Rolling Stand Electric Drive via SVPWM Algorithm with a Seven-Stage Switching Sequence
abstract: The aim of the article is to increase the energy efficiency of 5000 plate mill rolling stand electric drive based on a three-level (3L) neutral point clamped (NPC) voltage source inverter (VSI) via improved space-vector pulse-width modulation (SVPWM) algorithm. To achieve the goal, the paper proposes a new SVPWM algorithm with a seven-stage switching sequence. The developed mathematical model is implemented in the Matlab/Simulink. The total harmonic distortion (THD) factor for the established and suggested SVPWM algorithms is about 3.59% and 3.18% respectively. Thus, the deployment of the suggested SVPWM algorithm shall help significantly reduce power losses, which makes it a promising solution for energy efficiency improvement in metallurgy.

articleTitle: Development of a Model for Texture Analysis of Machined Parts on CNC Machines
abstract: This work is devoted to the development of a software module for analyzing the textures of machined parts on CNC machines using computer vision methods. The main goal of the research is to create a tool capable of analyzing geometric parameters of products based on texture properties of materials, which is especially relevant in the conditions of high-volume production. The paper considers modern methods of texture analysis, as well as their robustness to various disturbances such as illumination changes, noise, blurring, rotation and image scaling. An analysis system that combines binocular and texture methods of image processing is proposed, which makes it possible to improve the accuracy of measuring distances to objects on the basis of binocular algorithm, by means of additional analysis of texture properties of surfaces of the processed part.

articleTitle: Wireless Fire Safety Monitoring System
abstract: The development of modern industrial systems and their protection from emergencies is currently associated with the integration of wireless radio-electronic modules for monitoring the state of processes and devices that implement production processes. The use of wireless device communication technologies and fast data processing helps to increase the reliability of industrial systems, which is achieved by scanning devices and evaluating their parameters in real time. The use of IoT modules for wireless device management in human life safety systems is a priority, minimizing the impact of human error during emergencies in industrial IoT systems, as well as for special ones, such as those with a closed ecosystem. In this article, the authors analyzed the algorithms of microprocessor-based human life safety systems and the use of IoT solutions in security systems. A system for monitoring the condition of fire detectors has been developed. The intelligent module that scans the status of fire safety sensors is based on the K1986VE91T controller running on the cortex-m3 core. Data processing and statistics collection were implemented on a separate module based on the STM32F407VGT6 controller, with which the data collection device is in contact via wireless communication. Experimental data obtained on practical equipment confirmed the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms and the possibility of integration with existing fire safety systems.

articleTitle: A Genetic Approach to Ensuring the Reliability and Operational Efficiency of Distributed Data Storage in the Digital Industry
abstract: In the digital industry, the most promising and effective way to organize a distributed data storage is to use the distributed file system HDFS. The paper proposes an approach to ensuring the reliability and efficiency of distributed storage, which is based on optimizing the file distribution plan in the data storage, taking into account the criteria of reliability and operational efficiency. The proposed approach allows to reduce the response time of the storage system to requests. This is achieved in such a way that the indicator of operational efficiency tends to the maximum, and the reliability indicator is subject to restrictions corresponding to the requirements. The proposed approach consists of four stages: preparation of initial data, formation of preferred file distribution plans at the stages of design and reconfiguration of the storage, search for the optimal file distribution plan, distribution (redistribution) of files among storage nodes in accordance with the optimal distribution plan. Experimental evaluation of the proposed approach confirmed its high efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on High Voltage Safety Risk Prediction Model on Ships Using Artificial Neural Networks and Virtual Reality Technology
abstract: Currently, high-voltage electrical systems are used on ships to increase the ability to transport goods and reduce environmental emissions. High-voltage electrical equipment can cause danger when crew members work and come into contact. Therefore, training and coaching crew members with essential knowledge and skills is necessary to work with this voltage level. This paper presents a model of testing actual flashover voltage under the environment on ships based on the TERCO test kit. A neural network (ANN) model was also developed for flashover voltage. Finally, a high-voltage electrical safety simulation system is built using virtual reality technology and the Unity 3D platform. The research results show that it meets the essential electrical safety training criteria for modern maritime crew members.

articleTitle: Utilizing Cloud Computing for Research and Optimization of Complex Physicochemical Processes
abstract: The paper presents the main stages of the software implementation of heuristic methods for solving optimization problems based on a mathematical model of chemical reaction kinetics. In the context of digital transformation in manufacturing and the Industry 4.0 concept, a key direction is the integration of cloud and high-performance computing into research processes. This enables the creation of digital tools that ensure highly efficient modeling of complex physicochemical systems. To optimize such complex systems, heuristic methods are chosen, grounded in principles of stochastic search and global optimization, which facilitate effective exploration of the solution space. The software implementation of several heuristic methods is integrated into the computational core of a developed cloud-based SaaS service, designed for comprehensive research and modeling of complex physicochemical systems. The computational tasks are run in a remote environment using Docker containerization technology, ensuring scalability and convenience in distributed data processing. The functionality of the created system is demonstrated through the study of the Michaelis-Menten enzymatic reaction kinetics-a classical model of biochemical kinetics widely used in scientific research.

articleTitle: Application of Evolutionary Algorithms to Enhance the Efficiency of Neural Networks and Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: This study examines approaches to hyperparameter optimization in machine learning and deep learning systems using genetic algorithms. Today, the success of neural networks and machine learning algorithms largely depends on the correct tuning of their hyper parameters. Traditional approaches, such as search networks and Bayesian optimization, can sometimes be inefficient for high-dimensional and complex models. This study analyzes the possibility of improving machine learning results by selecting hyper parameters based on the principles of natural evolution of genetic algorithms. The proposed methods are tested on practical problems related to neural networks, and the results of the research on performance indicators reveal opportunities for improving the accuracy and efficiency of predictions in machine learning and neural networks.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Advancing Electric Vehicles Security Leveraging CICEVSE2024
abstract: The emergence of Electric Vehicles (EVs) and related charging infrastructure marks a significant shift toward sustainable transportation solutions. However, the increasing deployment of Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE) has introduced a new landscape for cybersecurity challenges. To address this critical issue, we utilize machine learning techniques for enhancing EVSE security systems leveraging CICEVSE2024, a new and comprehensive dataset tailored to advancing research on EVSE security. The dataset provides detailed records of EVSE activities, capturing both benign operations and attacks like Reconnaissance, Backdoor, Cryptojacking, Denial of Service (DoS), etc. in multiple states. Our research focuses on analyzing the performance of machine learning algorithms for securing EVSE systems. This study uses two techniques, namely Host Anomaly Detection Model (HADM) and Power Anomaly Detection Model (PADM), wherein machine learning algorithms are used to identify and classify attack scenarios with high performance. This research emphasizes the prospects of machine learning technologies in fortifying EVSE systems against cybersecurity threats, thereby contributing to the broader goal of ensuring the resilience of clean energy powered transportation solutions.

articleTitle: Industrial 3D Printing Quality Control System Based on Machine Vision
abstract: The work is devoted to improving the efficiency of the 3D printing quality control using machine learning and network technologies. Its relevance stems from the inherent limitations of quality control systems in additive manufacturing and the need to refine machine vision methods, models, and algorithms to automate and improve the control of the additive manufacturing process for technical products. Significant practical results have been obtained, demonstrating the effectiveness of a machine learning-based web service for 3D printing quality control. According to the results of calculating metrics for assessing the effectiveness of the proposed solution to classification and detection problems within the framework of a computational experiment, the F1-measure indicator is 0.94.

articleTitle: Rationale for the Applicability of the PULSE Data Transfer Protocol for Use in Predictive Diagnostic Systems for Complex Technical Equipment
abstract: The article considers modern tasks of collecting and interpreting data on the state of technical equipment, prospects for integrating various types of sensors and protocols into a single information network within the framework of the Internet of Things (IoT) and Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) technologies, as well as features of using predictive analytics methods to ensure operating regulations based on the actual state. The key technical difficulties associated with differences in polling speed, data volumes and protocol incompatibility are presented. The developed Pulse protocol and the Signalogic platform are described, providing efficient data processing, process automation and the ability to create a digital layer of the enterprise. The results of comparative tests of the performance of the Pulse protocol with MQTT are presented, demonstrating its superiority in signal processing speed. Examples of successful application of the developed solutions in industry are considered, including control systems for mining and processing equipment, as well as hazardous waste disposal. Particular attention is paid to the potential of predictive analytics in IoT and IIoT for predicting malfunctions, optimizing production processes and increasing equipment reliability. The paper describes the prospects for using machine learning technologies, real-time data analysis, and virtual stands for developing and testing systems. The paper highlights the importance of an interdisciplinary approach for the further development of IoT integration technologies that combine analytical, UX design, and engineering solutions.

articleTitle: Neural Network Implementation of the Probabilistic Detector in the Digital Stabilizer of Distorted Pulse Sequences
abstract: The paper contains the description on how to replace the Bayesian detector (“probabilistic relay”) in the developed digital stabilizer of the distorted pulse sequences by its neural network implementation. The main idea has been inspired by the proven abilities of neural networks to tune their weight coefficients in more flexible way providing improved accuracy for estimated parameters. As in the previous case, there are considered the pulse sequences being under affect by multiplicative and low frequency interferences along with the additive noise.
