The simulation modeling results have shown that under the same noise variances and interferences' behavior, the usage of the neural network implementation allows decreasing the mean square errors of pulse amplitude stabilization and improving the pulses' form restoration with 5–7 % comparing to the “classical” implementation of the detector as a computing routine procedure.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Machine Learning Effectiveness in Classifying Cracks on Foundry Product Images
abstract: This article presents an analysis of the effectiveness of machine learning methods for classifying cracks on foundry product images. The study focuses on evaluating the model's ability to adequately determine the level of risk, which is critical for ensuring industrial safety and improving production efficiency. The model's performance was assessed using metrics such as accuracy, recall, and F1-score, as well as through the analysis of ROC curves and the area under the curves (AUC), providing a detailed examination of its performance under various conditions. The results of the study indicate a high potential for the model's integration into production lines; however, additional adjustments will be required to minimize false positives, including the application of fuzzy logic and the integration of non-destructive testing methods. The proposed methods and achieved results can be applied to the development of automated quality control systems in mechanical engineering and other industries to timely identify and prevent risks associated with casting quality.

articleTitle: Data Anonymisation in Industrial Big Data Systems
abstract: Digital industrial systems widely use big data and data-driven technologies to create digital twins, analyse, control, and apply artificial intelligence techniques in manufacturing. Data anonymisation is an emerging method for ensuring privacy in modern big data systems. The paper highlights the features of technological data that are important in terms of obfuscation (anonymisation) methods. The authors have analysed the methods of anonymisation problem formulation. The paper shows that the anonymisation of technological data can use their properties due to the state of the described data-driven environment, equipment and processes in indirect anonymisation. An example of using intermediate states based on Markov models in providing differential privacy of industrial data is given and its advantage is shown.

articleTitle: Classification of Vehicle Motion and Immobility States Based on MEMS Accelerometer Signal
abstract: The algorithms of immobilizer operation in automobile security systems assume the presence of an autonomous speed sensor in the immobilizer. Given strict price restrictions, the speed sensor is implemented on a MEMS accelerometer. Calculating the speed requires determining the moments of time of changing the state of immobility to motion, and vice versa. The spectral composition of vibration accelerations, which is individual for each car, requires an individual approach, so it is advisable to use machine classification methods to determine the change of states. The classification model is configured and operated based on a vector of features whose numerical value is different in the states of motion and rest. Such features are usually called informative. It is proposed to use ranking methods to select the three most informative features from the full set of features, which constitute the input vector of the supervised classification model. The results of feature ranking based on the results of test drives of two cars with two different accelerometer locations are presented. It is shown that, as applied to the problem under consideration, the Bhattacharyya and ROC methods give the best results.

articleTitle: The Digital Equivalent of a Measuring Bridge for Complex Technical Systems
abstract: Measuring the degree of deformation of solids is a necessary measure in many areas of science. Sensor equipment containing load cells can perform such a measurement. This type of sensor uses a special type of resistor - a strain gauge. Various ways to incorporate these electronic components into the load cell circuit are described in this article. Using linear equations, numerical characteristics are calculated for different switching options, for example, the sensor sensitivity. Considered schemes for connecting different numbers of active and compensating strain gages to the measuring bridge are considered. Of or different types of deformation, it is necessary to apply suitable switching methods, this should be taken into account when designing information-measuring and control systems. A strain gauge is a resistor with a non-constant active resistance that varies within certain limits under the influence of mechanical loads (for example, when compressing, stretching, or bending the radio element in question). This type of resistor has found active application in sensor equipment, where it is used as a component of devices that recordtheir deformation of various structural elements, their displacement and mechanical stresses. One of the most common applications of a load cell in everyday life is a measuring scale. In the equipment under consideration, the strain gauges is included in the Whitson measuring bridge. In this article, we will present various ways to include strain gages in a bridge.

articleTitle: Model of the Protected Information Infrastructure for Assessing the Level of Information Security
abstract: As the number of information infrastructure objects and security measures increases, the likelihood of incorrect security level assessment also rises, leading to a higher risk of successful cyberattacks. The key challenges affecting assessment accuracy include data fragmentation across different security monitoring systems, data inconsistency or loss during integration, and difficulties in aggregating heterogeneous data over time. This paper proposes an ontological approach to modeling the protected information infrastructure, providing a formalized and structured description of internal security indicators. The developed ontology enables the representation of infrastructure components, their interrelations, security measures, and associated evidence and artifacts, such as vulnerability reports and event logs. The use of a knowledge graph allows for semantic analysis, identification of security control gaps, and risk assessment of vulnerabilities affecting critical components.

articleTitle: Research Intelligent Methods and Machine Learning Algorithms for Identification Anomalies in the Drilling Operations
abstract: Intelligent methods can analyze large volumes of data coming from a digital twin and identify bottlenecks in technological processes. Digital twins provide the ability to conduct scenario analysis and forecast various situations within technological processes. The use of digital twins and algorithms based on machine learning and data analysis helps improve product quality by identifying anomalies and problems at early stages, thereby allowing you to promptly make the necessary changes, which significantly reduces the time and financial costs of implementing the final product. Intelligent decision support systems can provide recommendations based on data analysis, both retrospective and received in real time, which significantly simplifies solving complex problems and improves the quality of decisions made. Thus, the integration of intelligent decision support methods and algorithms with digital twins can significantly improve the productivity, competitiveness and innovation of oil and gas enterprises. As part of the study, we analyzed the most suitable machine learning methods and algorithms for data labeling aimed at identifying anomalies in the process of stirring.

articleTitle: The Use of Digital Twins in the Energy Sector: Selection and Verification of Tools for Modeling Hybrid Energy Supply Systems Based on Renewable Energy Sources
abstract: The aim of the work is to develop and test a set of measures to improve the efficiency of projects for the construction of hybrid energy complexes with power plants based on renewable energy sources by using digital twins. The paper shows the effectiveness of research and development of recommendations on the choice of parameters and modes of operation of hybrid power complexes having a diverse composition of generating plants and high dependence on natural uncertain factors at all stages of the life cycle using the developed universal digital twin, which was verified by the example of real power complexes with different equipment composition.

articleTitle: Mathematical and Simulation Models of the External Power Supply System During Three-Phase Short Circuits in the External Network
abstract: This article presents the results of the study on the characteristics of residual voltage that occurs during three-phase short circuits in external networks of 110–220 kV. The research is based on the decomposition of the power supply scheme relatively the busbars of the system-forming substation into two parts: the external grid and power supply utility. The decomposition of the power supply system had led to the investigation of the residual voltages generated during three-phase short circuits and facilitated the identification of their characteristics. The paper provides parameters (magnitude of the initial component, decay constant) of the non-periodic component of the residual voltage and demonstrates their dependencies on network parameters, the location, and the phase of the short circuit occurrence. The obtained results enabled the formulation of a mathematical model of the external power supply grid. This mathematical model was used to develop a simulation model of the external power supply grid. The simulation model was based on an active four-pole terminal network in the Matlab (Simulink) environment.

articleTitle: Research and Development of Kubernetes Operator for Machine Learning Pipelines
abstract: The current research work addresses the problem of automating the delivery of machine learning models from MLflow to Kubernetes infrastructure. To solve the mentioned problem, a Kubernetes operator has been developed to automate the delivery of machine learning models to production by integrating MLflow for model tracking and Seldon Core for model serving. The developed operator allows data scientists to deploy models while maintaining the familiar MLflow environment. The operator's automatic deployment triggers upon tagging models in MLflow, greatly simplifying engineers' tasks and minimizing the need for manual infrastructure configuration. By automating configuration tasks and optimizing deployment workflows, the solution achieves a 40-50% reduction in model time to deployment (TTD) metric compared to manual processes and decreases error rates from 15% to around 3%. The practical relevance of the work is that it simplifies collaboration between data and infrastructure teams by providing a unified deployment framework, resulting in faster, more reliable, and automated integration of machine learning models into an organisation's business processes.

articleTitle: Combined Approach to Signature Verification Based on Fourier Transform, Hough Transform, Radon Transform, and the Support Vector Machine Method
abstract: This article presents a comprehensive and systematized methodology for applying advanced digital image processing techniques to address the challenges of signature verification. The authors conduct an in-depth investigation of Fourier, Hough, and Radon transform algorithms, which are utilized to extract distinctive and characteristic features from signature images. The study evaluates the contribution of these algorithms to enhancing the accuracy of authentication processes, providing a detailed analysis of their effectiveness in different scenarios. By combining theoretical reasoning with extensive experimental data, the authors develop a robust software platform designed for various stages of the signature verification process. This platform includes modules for training and test sample preparation, image preprocessing, extraction of unique features, and subsequent classification using the support vector method (SVM). The experimental results highlight the high efficiency of the proposed approach, demonstrating its ability to significantly improve the accuracy and reliability of signature verification. The findings suggest that the methodology has strong potential for practical applications in document security and biometric identification systems, where the need for reliable authentication is critical. The article also discusses the limitations of the current approach and outlines potential directions for future research, including the integration of machine learning techniques and the exploration of additional feature extraction methods to further enhance performance.

articleTitle: Automated Detection and Localization of Wind Turbine Deformations Through YOLO11 and UAV Systems
abstract: This study presents an advanced model for the automated detection of turbine blade deformations, leveraging Industry 4.0 technologies such as machine learning, computer vision, and GPS-based localization. The majority of the dataset used for training the model was created with a UAV system equipped with a high-resolution camera, enabling precise and comprehensive data collection from turbine blades during routine inspections. YOLO11 model was trained to identify and classify common turbine blade deformations, including cracks, surface wear, blade bending, and thermal deformations. By integrating GPS support, the UAV system detects deformations and accurately pinpoints their locations, facilitating efficient and targeted maintenance interventions. The model achieved an overall precision of over 80%, demonstrating robust performance in detecting visible deformations such as cracks and blade bending. However, challenges persist in identifying smaller deformations, such as fine cracks and surface roughness, which underline the need for dataset augmentation and enhanced training methods. This study underscores the transformative potential of AI-driven UAV systems in predictive maintenance, contributing to the digital evolution of the wind energy sector. By integrating automation, real-time data processing, and advanced analytics, the approach aligns with Smart Industry and Industry 4.0 principles, promoting operational efficiency, cost savings, and sustainability.

articleTitle: Methods for Identifying Implicit Communities and Analyzing Social Networks Using AI
abstract: The article provides an overview of modern methods and algorithms for detecting hidden communities in social networks, a crucial task given the rapid growth of data volumes and the complexity of network structures. The analysis covers clustering approaches and structural characterization of social graphs, including label propagation algorithms, density-based methods, as well as modularity and distributed computing algorithms. The paper explores the identification of implicit connections among users formed by shared interests, social environments, or behavioral patterns. A comprehensive evaluation of approaches to modeling network structures and interpreting interpersonal connections is provided, leveraging text content analysis, social interaction, and influence metrics. Challenges in computational efficiency and algorithm convergence for large-scale data analysis are discussed, alongside proposed improvements for testing and validation methods. Experimental studies validate the developed algorithms on various social graph structures, including real-world and synthetic data, highlighting the influence of topological and behavioral factors on community detection quality. The paper also describes some methods and algorithms for analysing users and communities.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of the Two-Stage Hybrid Anomaly Detection Model for ICS Subjected to Cyberattacks
abstract: This study presents a performance comparison of a proposed two-staged hybrid anomaly detection model with several state-of-the-art models in the context of industrial control systems under the influence of cyberattacks. Developed hybrid method consists of two stages. In the first stage, hierarchical clustering is performed to create a dendrogram from the raw data. The resulting dendrogram is then cut on a variable level when the data is clustered without mixing normal and anomalous data. In the second stage an ensemble of several unsupervised anomaly detection methods is used to determine the label for the clusters from the first stage. Evaluation of methods is made with SWaT and HAI datasets using common machine learning models metrics of performance. Proposed method demonstrated high performance for the task of determining the anomalous states for the SWaT dataset and comparable performance for the HAI dataset even with supervised anomaly detection methods.

articleTitle: Neural Network Architecture Search Algorithm for Technical Object State Prediction
abstract: The paper presents a new algorithm for automated search for neural network architecture for predicting the state of technical objects. Prediction is a key element of monitoring, allowing us to prevent accidents and improve the reliability of complex systems. The proposed approach combines the methods of Cartesian genetic programming, multi-criteria evolutionary algorithms and Bayesian optimization. This algorithm adapts neural network architectures to different types of data, speeds up the search for a suitable model configuration, and improves forecast accuracy. The developed algorithm was implemented as a standalone program in the Python programming language using the TensorFlow and Keras libraries. The effectiveness of the developed approach has been tested in practice in predicting the remaining service life of bearings, a turbojet engine, and a Li-ion battery. The AutoKeras library was used to compare the results. The study showed that the use of the developed algorithm significantly improves the performance quality of neural network models compared to the models obtained using the AutoKeras library. The algorithm demonstrated high accuracy of predictions, stability to various conditions, and potential for application in monitoring systems of technical objects.

articleTitle: Algorithms of a Multi-Position Radar System Using Neural Networks for Ornithological Safety Tasks
abstract: Detecting birds near airfields is one of the most urgent tasks of radars, as the number of aircraft collisions with birds is only increasing every year. In this article, we discuss the possibility of using neural networks to solve the problem of bird detection. The range of applications of neural network technologies in radar tasks is relevant, for example, in tasks of temporal and spectral filtering and object recognition. The main advantage of neural networks is that they can recognize deeper patterns in the data. In the learning process, neurons are able to respond to the information received in accordance with the principles of generalization, thereby solving the task assigned to them. In this article, the possibility of using neural networks as secondary signal processing will be analyzed for radar tasks. The paper analyzes two filtering algorithms: the first one is based on filtering the estimates of the state vector by Kalman, while the other algorithm uses an artificial neural network to predict the estimation of the state vector. For these secondary processing algorithms, an efficiency comparison based on location detection errors was performed. Experimental data obtained on the basis of a field experiment showed a slight gain in the accuracy of the neural algorithm over the Kalman filter and a loss in operational efficiency and computational costs.

articleTitle: Ontology-Driven Semantic Interoperability for Discrete Manufacturing
abstract: The paper proposes ontologies for planning assembly production and mechanical processing to support decision-making in managing a discrete manufacturing process. To obtain a complete picture of the technological process, it is necessary to ensure the systematic integration of all relevant data from several systems and devices based on knowledge of the production area. Semantic interoperability is ensured based on the implementation of the same ontology in interacting systems. The ontologies were created in the open Protégé system to establish correspondence between product manufacturing concepts when processing a knowledge base by translating data from the MES (Manufacturing Execution System) and the RDF file (Resource Description Framework). The architecture of the system using the knowledge base is proposed. An application in C# is considered, which is included in the system, reads operational values of technology implementation parameters and forms new triplets in the knowledge base. The difference of the proposed approach is, firstly, the ontological integration of assembly production and mechanical processing and, secondly, the consideration of operationally changing data transferred from the DBMS to the KBMS to support decision-making. The time of information transfer to the knowledge base and to the database were obtained; a comparison of average recording times is given. The created application and the developed ontologies can become the basis for creating digital twins for the discrete production process

articleTitle: Neural Network Method for Forecasting Time Series Discretized with Violation of the Kotelnikov-Shannon Theorem Requirements
abstract: The problem of restoring a continuous signal from a limited set of discrete values is in demand in automated digital production of Industry 4.0, controlled by artificial intelligence systems. When fulfilling the requirements of the Kotelnikov-Shannon theorem a continuous signal from discrete signal values is possible to be accurately reconstructed, however, in practice, situations, where there is a gap in discrete signal values or the discretization interval is random, often arise. The presented research results apply an engineering approach to the problem of reconstructing a continuous signal from its discrete signal values, which is not based on complex mathematical apparatus. The novelty of the research results lies in the proposed method of forecasting and restoring a continuous signal from a limited set of discrete values (time series) taken at random time moments, the mathematical expectation of which exceeds the value of the discretization interval specified by the Kotelnikov-Shannon theorem. The method is based on the use of an artificial neural network to obtain discrete signal values with a higher frequency than in the original set of discrete signal values of the time series. For this purpose, a stack of training data is formed for the neural network, including discrete signal values, interval discretization values, and the first and second differences of the time series values. The conducted model experiments with the program implementing the proposed method demonstrated its efficiency and high accuracy of the time series values obtained with its help with a regular discretization frequency satisfying the Kotelnikov-Shannon theorem.

articleTitle: Application of Machine Learning Methods for Production Data Analysis
abstract: Ensuring the quality of CNC-machined parts is a challenging task in modern manufacturing due to frequent shifts in production conditions and the high costs of traditional inspection methods. In this study, we propose a data-driven approach that integrates machine learning (ML) models with statistical acceptance sampling to dynamically optimize quality control processes. Production data from ERP, MES, and IIoT systems were analyzed with Gradient Boosting model. By continuously retraining the model on newly completed batches, the system adapts to evolving conditions, maintaining predictive accuracy. A key innovation of this work is the timely adjustment of sampling parameters (e.g., sample size, acceptance number) according to predicted defect levels. This adaptive strategy conserves inspection resources when defect risks are low and intensifies monitoring when risks are high. The results demonstrate a marked reduction in inspection costs and a robust capacity to detect defects promptly, aligning with industry goals of minimizing scrap and rework. Overall, this study validates the effectiveness of applying machine learning methods to production data analysis, laying a foundation for future enhancements in adaptive, proactive quality control systems.

articleTitle: Building a System of Analytics of Information Security Events in the Automated Process Control System and Incident Analysis Based on Cluster Analysis
abstract: The paper discusses the development and application of an ensemble model combining cluster analysis methods and neural networks to improve the efficiency of anomaly detection in network traffic of industrial ACSs. The focus is on the integration of clustering methods such as DBSCAN and HDBSCAN, which demonstrate high accuracy in detecting anomalies characteristic of different types of cyber attacks. A PDPC algorithm is proposed that improved the density clustering of DPC by using a particle swarm optimization technique, showing significant superiority over existing methods. Clustering approaches under training data constraints and complexity in information security risk assessment are also investigated. A web interface is developed to provide administrators with the ability to monitor and promptly respond to threats, as well as to control model parameters in real time. The results show that the proposed approach significantly strengthens the cybersecurity of industrial networks by adapting to dynamically changing environmental conditions.

articleTitle: Synthetic Data-Enhanced Microcrack Detection in Photovoltaic (PV) Cells Using YOLO11 for Smart Industry Applications
abstract: The recent advancements in smart industry and advanced automation are reshaping industries by introducing cutting-edge technologies that improve efficiency, sustainability, and productivity across sectors such as manufacturing, energy, and infrastructure. In particular, the application of automated systems for monitoring and maintenance tasks plays a crucial role in the optimization of industrial operations. One such area is the monitoring of photovoltaic (PV) cells, which are integral components of renewable energy systems. Detecting defects, such as microcracks, in these cells is critical for ensuring their efficiency and longevity. This study focuses on the use of object detection algorithms, specifically YOLO11, to identify and classify microcracks in PV cells. A key innovation in this research is the use of both real and synthetic crack images in training the detection model. By artificially creating cracks of varying sizes, orientations, and locations on PV cells, we expand the training dataset, improving the model's robustness and accuracy in detecting defects. The study also compares the performance of YOLO11 with previous versions of the YOLO algorithm, YOLOv8, YOLOv9, and YOLOv10, across multiple performance metrics, using both primary (real crack) and expanded (synthetic crack) datasets. The results demonstrate that YOLO11 achieves high precision and recall values, particularly for detecting large cracks, with notable improvements when the expanded dataset is utilized. The proposed work highlights the potential of advanced object detection algorithms in the context of smart industry and advanced automation, offering a scalable solution for real-time monitoring and maintenance of PV cells.

articleTitle: Innovative, Semi-Permanent Sensors in the Era of Industry 4.0: Technological Solutions for Efficient Monitoring and Automation
abstract: In the era of Industry 4.0, manufacturing and research environments demand increasingly sophisticated monitoring and diagnostic systems. Alongside traditional stationary and portable sensors, semi-permanent (hybrid) sensors have emerged to offer a balanced solution that leverages the high accuracy of fixed installations and the mobility of handheld devices. These hybrid sensors integrate seamlessly with wireless communication protocols, such as Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) and Wi-Fi etc, providing sufficient data throughput for moderate to high-frequency measurements (e.g., vibration analysis). Their adaptability allows rapid relocation, on-the-fly updates, and real-time data processing, reducing downtime and enhancing responsiveness in dynamic production workflows. Furthermore, the hybrid approach facilitates advanced analytics—such as machine learning algorithms and augmented reality (AR) overlays—without relying solely on dedicated, permanent instrumentation. Semi-permanent sensors address various operational challenges, including cost-effective deployment, compatibility with legacy systems, and centralized data management within ERP platforms. They are thus particularly beneficial for organizations aiming to accelerate digital transformation initiatives, improve predictive maintenance strategies, and minimize equipment failure risks. Although extremely harsh or specialized environments may still favor fully stationary or highly portable options, semi-permanent sensors strike an optimal balance of flexibility and reliability. As a result, they represent an effective foundation for modern condition-monitoring frameworks in Industry 4.0.

articleTitle: Automated Collection and Processing of Spatiotemporal Data for the Analysis of Sustainable Development in Industrial Systems
abstract: A software-analytical platform has been developed for the automated collection, structuring, and normalization of spatiotemporal data obtained from national statistical service web platforms. Algorithms for dynamic adaptation to changes in the DOM structure of web pages have been implemented, ensuring parsing resilience against modifications in HTML markup. Methods for bypassing anti-bot mechanisms have been introduced, including navigator.webdriver modification, User-Agent customization, and management of Chrome DevTools Protocol parameters. A data processing pipeline has been developed, incorporating semantic integrity verification, outlier removal, and transformation into a relational structure. Algorithm accuracy has been verified through manual validation of a randomly selected sample of 50 records, demonstrating a 98% match rate. The average data extraction speed reached 12.4 records per second. The results confirm the reproducibility of the methods, high adaptability to changes in web resources, and applicability in tasks related to the collection and processing of statistical data for analyzing the sustainable development of industrial systems. Future research is aimed at integrating machine learning for predictive analytics and enhancing computational efficiency in processing large-scale datasets.

articleTitle: Generation of Solutions in Spatial Situational Analysis of Logistic Projects
abstract: In a geoinformation system (GIS), a logistics project functions as an informational entity that describes the spatiotemporal processes required for generation and maintenance of material flows. Given the incomplete description of the interactions between the logistics project and its external environment, the application of case-based reasoning (CBR) becomes appropriate. CBR enables the resolution of anomalies in logistics processes by leveraging past experiences. This study addresses the problem of developing spatial representations of solutions for anomalous situations represented as two-component images. Such an image represents extended knowledge about a set of precedents within a limited territory. Beyond the precedent scheme on a map, the proposed approach incorporates new cartographic objects in the image, reflecting possible, permissible, and impermissible transformations of the situation. These transformations should be viewed as invariants of the situation's essence. Use of images improves decision-making reliability. For solution generation, the following approach is proposed: a spatial image is constructed for a problematic situation and compared with images stored in the intelligent GIS. The solution image of the most semantically similar situation is used as the foundation for generating solution options. The generation process involves transforming the solution image to fit the spatial area of the anomalous situation and forming a set of acceptable instances based on semantic content. This paper elucidates the principle of spatial transformation of images and explores methods for selecting the optimal solution. The advantages and limitations of the proposed solution generation method are analyzed using data from the OpenStreetMap geoinformation service.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Clustering Approaches for Text Embeddings
abstract: With the rapid growth of text data, effective automated analysis methods are essential. Text clustering helps uncover patterns and structure large datasets, but existing algorithms face challenges due to high-dimensional text representations from language models. This study compares clustering algorithms to evaluate their strengths, weaknesses and applicability. The research examines partition-based, hierarchical and density-based clustering, analyzing k-means, agglomerative clustering and DBSCAN on the 20Newsgroups dataset. Performance is assessed using key clustering quality metrics. Results show that k-means effectively captures data structure, while DBSCAN struggles with high-dimensional text data. The study highlights the impact of distance metrics on clustering outcomes and provides recommendations for improving algorithm performance in text analysis. This research is valuable for professionals in automated text processing and machine learning. It offers practical insights into selecting suitable clustering methods based on task requirements and data characteristics, enhancing text analysis in fields such as IT, marketing and analytics.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Programming Environment for Recognition of Metallurgical Production Objects in Real Time
abstract: The article is devoted to the creation and testing of a programming environment for an automatic identification system for steel sheets in metallurgical production based on the analysis of unique biometric features. The proposed solution ensures detection of a representative surface area and its subsequent recognition as the object moves along the process line. The proposed approach eliminates dependence on external markers, such as QR codes or tags, due to a detailed study of the surface texture, defect distribution and rolling patterns. To optimize the neural network model and simulate real operating conditions, a production line model was used that takes into account variable parameters such as lighting, object movement and image noise level. An important aspect of the study is a solution that allows performing recognition functions in real time and provides end-to-end integration of the system with adjacent industrial MES and SCADA platforms via the REST API.

articleTitle: Enhancing Solar Power Forecasting in Abuja: An Application of XAI Techniques for Improved Transparency and Trust
abstract: The increasing integration of photovoltaic (PV) power into energy grids necessitates accurate forecasting to enhance grid stability and optimize energy management. However, traditional machine learning models often lack interpretability, leading to concerns regarding reliability and trust in AI-driven predictions. This study applies Explainable AI (XAI) techniques, including SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME), and feature importance plots, to improve the transparency of a hybrid Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator-Random Forest Regression (LASSO-RFR) model for PV power forecasting in Abuja, Nigeria. By analyzing meteorological datasets from 2020–2022, the hybrid model was evaluated using key performance metrics such as Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and R-squared <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{R}^{2})$</tex>. The results indicate that the hybrid LASSO-RFR framework enhances prediction accuracy while maintaining model interpretability. XAI analyses revealed that surface pressure, dew point temperature, and air temperature were the most influential variables in forecasting solar radiation. The findings underscore the importance of integrating XAI tools into AI-driven energy forecasting models to improve transparency, stakeholder confidence, and practical deployment in real-world scenarios.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Autonomous Navigation of Service Robots in Complex Industrial Environments with SAR-Based Vision and Advanced Detection for Industry 4.0
abstract: In the era of Industry 4.0 and Smart Industry, the integration of autonomous systems into industrial operations offers promising advancements in safety, efficiency, and productivity. This paper presents a novel methodology for navigating service robots, specifically unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs), within challenging industrial environments where visibility is often limited, and obstacles are abundant. Our approach employs a combination of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) simulation and dark channel processing to enhance low-light images, followed by edge extraction to accurately distinguish ground and horizon levels. The methodology further integrates the YOLO11 algorithm to identify and remove obstacles, enabling the UGV to focus on navigable paths. Finally, we apply a random point assignment and linear regression approach to generate a potential route, guiding the service robot through unstructured and dynamic industrial landscapes. The proposed method was tested on a dataset of 591 images captured in simulated industrial settings, revealing high accuracy in route generation with minimal deviation from ground-truth paths. The YOLO11 algorithm achieved a precision of 90.3% in identifying and excluding obstacles, ensuring safe and efficient path planning. The findings indicate that this methodology effectively addresses the navigational challenges faced by service robots in complex environments, aligning with the goals of Industry 4.0 by advancing the autonomy and operational resilience of industrial robotic systems.

articleTitle: Recognition Algorithm of Carbon Chains in Nanoparticle Assemblies from Electron Microscopy Images
abstract: This paper presents the results of the development and application of neural networks for the automated analysis of images obtained from an electron microscope to recognize gold nanoparticles and carbyne chains. The YOLOv4 architecture, trained on 5 annotated images, was used to solve the nanoparticle detection task. The model demonstrated stable results with a loss function of 1.6, indicating its high accuracy in object localization. To detect connections between particles, the YOLOv8 architecture was applied, trained on 13 images with polygonal masks. The model exhibited high efficiency in segmenting connections, as confirmed by the Precision, Recall, and F1-score metrics. However, difficulties were encountered in detecting small particles and connections under low contrast conditions, requiring further optimization. Testing on test data confirmed the models' functionality, although cases of false positives and missed detections were noted. Future work suggests employing more advanced architectures, such as YOLO11, as well as increasing the volume and diversity of training data to enhance model accuracy and robustness. The developed solutions can be used to accelerate the analysis of nanostructures in materials science, nanoengineering, and other scientific fields.

articleTitle: Simulation of Radiation Non-Destructive Testing Operations Based on Virtual Reality and the NDE 4.0 Paradigm
abstract: The implementation of digital industrial technologies marks a pivotal step towards maximizing automation in production processes, aligning with the principles of Industry 4.0 and the NDE 4.0 paradigms. One key area of focus is the modeling of radiation non-destructive evaluation operations within a virtual reality framework. This innovative approach allows for the creation and software application of simulators specifically designed for non-destructive testing of various materials and products. In this context, a complex multi-component digital twin of radiographic image is proposed. The digital twin serves as a comprehensive virtual model that mirrors the characteristics and behaviors of its physical counterpart. The images are generated using discrete modeling techniques that utilize both fundamental physical principles and empirical data provided by manufacturers. This dual approach ensures that the resulting radiographic images closely resemble those produced during actual X-ray inspections. One of the spatial factors that affects image sharpness and quality of inspection is also included in the model. By utilizing virtual reality and digital twin technologies, radiation non-destructive testing training becomes more efficient and better aligned with the automation goals of contemporary industrial practices.

articleTitle: ASD (Autistic Spectrum Disorder) Preschool Children Socialization Using Experimental Monitored Virtual Environments
abstract: The paper presents the development and testing of a virtual reality (VR) application for the development of social skills in preschool children with autistic spectrum disorders (ASD). The application includes a system of adaptive learning scenarios based on traditional methods of working with children with ASD, an interactive virtual assistant with an advanced navigation system and based on hand gesture recognition. Special attention was paid to the development of an automatic report generation system based on the Childhood Autism Rating Scale (CARS), which analyses more than 10 different parameters of user interaction with the virtual environment to track the dynamics of the condition. These reports form the basis for analysing user interaction with the virtual environment, which is especially important for the therapy of children with ASD, as it allows to adapt the training methodology to the individual characteristics of each child and adjust the therapeutic process based on objective progress indicators. The network interaction possibility was implemented to control the therapy process in real time, including visualisation of the user's movement trajectory and analysis of the visited zones of the virtual space. Initial testing was carried out on a control group of three normotypical 4–5 year old children to collect reference values of interaction with the virtual environment.

articleTitle: Protection Efficiency Evaluation for Blockchain-Based Subsytems of a Smart City
abstract: An unclear security perimeter, low level of end node security, combined with the increased activity of intruders using advanced techniques to bypass security systems, significantly complicate the task of ensuring cybersecurity of blockchain-based digital infrastructures on smart city. To reduce cyber risks affecting smart city, various protection mechanisms with configured rules for correlating events in the distributed digital infrastructure are used. However, due to the dynamics of the protected object and the rapidly changing landscape of cyberthreats, assessing the effectiveness of the defense mechanisms and selecting the optimal configuration is a complex task. This paper presents a developed mathematical model of cybersecurity event management using a continuous-time Markov chain, within which the problem to be solved is to prevent the system from transitioning from the state of “a cybersecurity event occurred” to the state of “a cybersecurity incident occurred” due to high accuracy and speed of detection and response to the event. This paper also presents a developed model of the cyberattack propagation in blockchain-based subsystems of a smart city based on the extension of the traditional predator-prey model, within which a criterion of adequacy of applied protective mechanisms to the changing parameters of the smart city system and current cyberthreats is proposed. The experimental study has confirmed prospects of the suggested solution in assessing the effectiveness and selecting the optimal configuration of the protection system.

articleTitle: A Discrete Swarm Optimization Modification for the Multi-Agent Traveling Salesman Problem
abstract: The paper presents a discrete modification of the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm aimed at solving the multi-agent Traveling Salesman Problem (mTSP) under a minimax objective. By representing city permutations as “positions” and exchange sequences as “velocities,” the standard PSO framework is adapted to effectively handle discrete routing tasks. Experimental results show that the proposed approach substantially reduces the longest individual route across various numbers of agents <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(m)$</tex> and particle counts <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(N)$</tex>, with larger swarms achieving greater improvements. The method proves both flexible and robust, capable of distributing travel loads among multiple salesmen while maintaining competitive solution quality. Future extensions may incorporate additional constraints or multi-objective formulations, further enhancing its applicability to complex logistics and scheduling problems.

articleTitle: Optimization of Identification, Recognition and Prediction of Non-Stationary Objects Based on Tools for Monitoring and Correcting Distorted Information
abstract: Scientific and methodological foundations have been developed for optimal identification, recognition, and forecasting of random time series of non-stationary objects based on tools for detecting and correcting distorted information. Mechanisms for optimizing identification are proposed, involving the use of tools for extracting and using textural, specific characteristics of information. A wide range of mechanisms for tracking, identifying characteristic areas, detecting and correcting distorted information based on the tools of basis functions of Fourier transform and filtering under the condition of internal and external influences, the presence of noise (interference), blurring of points, various defects, a priori limitations and uncertainty have been studied. A mechanism based on graph embedding in vector space and the Young-Householder transformation method have been developed. Mechanisms that represent random time series by vectors of numerical characteristics, spectral characteristics, a search graph, and use decompositions of the normalized Laplace matrix have been studied and implemented. Solutions of the thermal kernel equations are obtained using the eigenvalues and vectors of the Laplace matrix. The effectiveness of identifying a non-stationary object has been studied on the basis of mechanisms using parabolic, orthogonal algebraic polynomial, linear autoregressive model, Daubechies 4 interpolation polynomial, cubic interpolation spline function, and three-layer neural network. A software package was implemented, the modules of which were created in the C++ language in the parallel computing environment “CUDA”.

articleTitle: Autoencoders and Multidimensional Clustering Algorithms in the Identification of Engineering-Geological Elements
abstract: The article investigates the use of modern machine learning techniques in engineering geological analysis. Key methods include autoencoders for dimensionality reduction and uncovering hidden patterns, alongside clustering algorithms (k-means, fuzzy c-means, DBSCAN, GMM, and Self-Organizing Map (SOM)) to identify engineering geological elements (EGEs). Indicator kriging is utilized for spatial interpolation of categorical data. The study analyzes a dataset of 90 soil samples, focusing on parameters such as soil density, modulus of deformation, and internal friction angle, using PCA, Variance Threshold, and correlation analysis for feature selection. Among clustering algorithms, k-means demonstrated the best results (silhouette score = 0.635, Davies-Bouldin index = 0.454), making it ideal for soil transitional layers. Fuzzy c-means and DBSCAN showed advantages for transitional zones and irregular densities, respectively. Indicator kriging produced detailed spatial cross-sections using an exponential variogram, significantly reducing modeling uncertainty. Autoencoders without intermediate layers achieved high reconstruction accuracy (R2 = 0.72, MSE = 0.02), effectively supporting clustering in latent space. The study emphasizes the importance of proper normalization, particularly for heterogeneous datasets, and highlights the potential of machine learning to improve classification, interpolation, and spatial modeling of EGEs. Future research should address autoencoder sensitivity to normalization and explore feature selection techniques, such as random forests, to enhance robustness and scalability.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Framework for Forecasting Air Quality Index
abstract: Air pollution involves complex interactions between meteorological factors, emissions, geographical features, and human activities. Traditional statistical models often struggle to capture these non-linear and multi-dimensional relationships, while Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) models are superior at this. Accurate predictions and insights from ML and DL models enable policymakers to implement timely interventions, such as issuing health advisories, optimizing traffic, and controlling industrial emissions. This study explores the application of ML and DL models to predict Air Quality Index (AQI) using a dataset collected from one of air polluted cities in the world - Tashkent, the capital of Uzbekistan. The problem is analyzed a classification task using the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest (RF), Decision Tree (DT), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) with different optimizers such as Adam, AdaGrad, RMSprop, SGD with momentum. Performance metrics, including Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1-Score are utilized to evaluate model performance. The results exhibit the strengths and limitations of different models and offer insights into the most suitable approaches for AQI prediction.

articleTitle: Machine Learning in Defectoscopy: DBSCAN for Localization, Agglomerative Clustering for Typification
abstract: Acoustic emission (AE) is one of the most relevant and cost-effective non-destructive testing methods for identifying defects in industrial objects. This paper addresses two primary tasks in defectoscopy: locating hazardous AE zones and classifying signals according to the presumed defect type. Through our research, we have determined and experimentally confirmed that the most suitable machine learning method for localization is a modified DBSCAN, while Agglomerative Clustering is optimal for typification. This paper details the specific tuning and modifications applied to these methods for AE. The resulting models were successfully tested on real-world data. The accuracy of the localization results was assessed using statistical analysis and consultations with AE experts, while typification was validated probabilistically and tested on sample data.

articleTitle: Visualization Method for Visual Analysis of Security Data Using Neural Networks
abstract: The aim of this study is to develop a method for creating effective visualization models that can generate graphs from security data for later visual analysis using artificial intelligence methods. This study systematically analyzes the areas of information security where neural networks are applied, and presents the most common neural network architectures used for image analysis. To develop the method, conceptual visualization models are proposed that take into account the technical features of convolutional neural networks and the differences in perception between human operators and neural networks. The method is based on these conceptual models and a set of visual design principles. This approach will allow one to not only design visualization models suitable for neural network analysis but also automate the work of human operators. The proposed solution can play an important role in developing information security applications. The study also suggests an architecture for a software prototype based on the proposed method. The findings of this study may be useful for developers of decision support systems and researchers working in the field of neural network technology.

articleTitle: Enhancing IoT-Driven Garbage Analysis in Smart Cities Through Interpretable CNN Feature Maps
abstract: In the contemporary era, the pressing challenge for an increasingly urbanized society is the transformation of cities into technological green islands that facilitate a peaceful and sustainable lifestyle for their inhabitants. Among the myriad of issues plaguing large metropolises, the accumulation of uncollected waste stands out as a critical concern that not only detracts from the aesthetic appeal of urban environments but also poses significant health and environmental risks. Fortunately, advancements in modern computer vision systems have reached a level of sophistication that empowers them to efficiently identify and classify waste through photographs captured by surveillance cameras. This paper undertakes a comprehensive evaluation of the application of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) as a foundational element for developing a garbage detection system based on image data from streets. We delve into various architectural strategies for constructing an IoT solution that seamlessly integrates a high-resolution camera, a compact microcomputer, a pre-trained neural network, and a service for incorporation into a smart city cloud infrastructure. To elucidate the inner workings of the neural network and its interpretative processes at various layers, we employ advanced visualization techniques to generate feature maps for all object classes relevant to our study. We show that a CNN used for garbage classification acts in a bio-inspired way.

articleTitle: Approach to Forming Vulnerability Datasets for Fine-Tuning AI Agents
abstract: This study addresses the problem of identifying vulnerabilities in open-source code by exploring existing methods of code analysis and evaluating the feasibility of automating security assessments using large language models (LLMs). We propose an approach for constructing high-quality datasets to fine-tune LLMs for software security analysis. Our methodology involves collecting and processing vulnerability data, filtering and curating security-related code changes, and structuring datasets to optimize model fine-tuning. We present an algorithm for aggregating vulnerability data sources and constructing a dataset specifically for training security-focused LLMs. To validate our approach, we fine-tune models from the Qwen family for software vulnerability detection in Python codebases during development and testing. Our findings demonstrate that the proposed method enables the development of intelligent, continuously adaptable AI agents capable of identifying and analyzing emerging zero-day vulnerabilities, not only in Python but also in other structurally similar programming languages.

articleTitle: Text Tone Analysis in Social Networks: Research, Evaluation and Comparison of Algorithm Performance
abstract: The article is devoted to a comprehensive study of methods for analyzing the tonality of textual information in order to improve the effectiveness of information security monitoring and public opinion management in the digital environment. The authors conduct a comparative analysis of approaches based on lexicographic methods, machine learning with a teacher (naive Bayesian classifier and maximum entropy method) and systems using a set of rules. The study includes a detailed review of the algorithmic features, advantages and limitations of each method, as well as an evaluation of their adaptability when the topics of the analyzed texts change. The results of the comparative analysis show that machine learning methods demonstrate higher performance in terms of accuracy, completeness and F-measure compared to rule set based systems. The authors also draw attention to the dependence of the results on the specifics of the training sample and the peculiarities of the contextual application of algorithms. The practical significance of the work lies in the possibility of using the developed methods for the rapid detection of negative content and predicting changes in classification accuracy when adapting to new topics, which is especially relevant for information security and management decision support in a dynamically developing digital environment.

articleTitle: Social Engineering Cyberattack Model
abstract: The problem of cybersecurity against SE methods remains relevant annually. Applying organizational and software security methods to protect user does not achieve the desired result, since this is the last defensive line. Furthermore, present articles do not pay enough attention to the protection of the communication channel, which made the attack possible, to countering the attacker and the prerequisites for the first stage of the attack. To implement this concept, a detailed description of a social engineering attack and the characteristics of the attacker is necessary, which will allow the application of countermeasures to provide cybersecurity. This work provides an analysis of existing approaches to describing social engineering methods. Advantages and disadvantages of descriptions in each article have been presented. The main section of this article provides a description of social engineering methods using the mathematical elements of set theory. Set-theoretic models describe the properties of entities of social engineering attacks. The article also provides a description of the interaction between models, methods of counteracting attack actions at each stage. An example of a description of the attack process using set theory is given.

articleTitle: Possibility of Implementing the Concept of a Unmanned Small Hydroelectric Power Plant from the Point of View of Information Security
abstract: The concept of unmanned operation of small hydroelectric power plants is proposed in this paper. This concept ensures unconditional compliance with all applicable requirements of regulatory and technical documentation governing the operation of hydroelectric power plants. The assessment of technical feasibility (taking into account the current and prospective level of technology development) and risks (taking into account previously identified limitations and barriers), as well as possible consequences of the implementation of the concept: economic (in terms of the impact on operating costs), social (in terms of the impact on the availability of labor resources, the impact on the level of employment etc.), technical (in terms of the impact on the reliability of facilities and power supply to consumers), is also carried out. It was made a conclusion about the possibility of implementing this concept from the point of view of ensuring its information security.

Author Keywords: the concept of unmanned operation of small hydroelectric power plants

articleTitle: Algorithms for Image Processing of Micro-Objects of Medical Diagnostics Systems
abstract: Constructive approaches, principles, models for optimizing the identification of micro-objects based on the use of statistical, dynamic models with mechanisms for filtering noise, foreign particles on images of medical objects and pollen grains have been developed. Methods for optimizing the identification of micro-objects with the selection of characteristic objects in the image, the combination of image models with the mechanisms of segmentation, filtering, transformation, and alignment of the laser image processing zone with the CAD model are proposed. Algorithms for selecting the contours of objects on an image using a border detector in the transverse direction to each vector of the CAD model have been developed. Modeling of images of microsamples for medical diagnostics of chest diseases was carried out. The width, straightness of the boundaries of structural objects, local defects, parameters of regulation and synchronization of the components of the vision system are determined. Algorithms for image processing under conditions of a priori insufficiency, uncertainty of parameters, and low accuracy of data processing are studied. A mechanism for suppressing impulse noise and noise is implemented based on various filtering methods, preserving the boundaries of objects and small-sized parts. Mathematical expressions for estimating identification errors due to non-stationarity, inadequacy of approximation, interpolation, extrapolation of the image contourare obtained, which are synthesized with cubic, biquadratic, interpolation spline functions and wavelet transforms. A software package for recognition and classification of micro-objects has been developed.

articleTitle: Prevention of Selfish Mining Attacks in Blockchain-Enabled Smart City Networks
abstract: The paper presents a method for protecting a blockchain against selfish mining attacks. The mining algorithm in blockchains with the Proof-of-Work consensus has been investigated. Related works in the area of detecting selfish mining attacks are reviewed. A selfish miner has an advantage in profitability with a hash rate of more than 25% of the network capacity. Detection of selfish mining attacks is based on analyzing the behavior of a mining pool. Stratum V2 protocol message fields are identified that allow detecting a selfish mining attack from a mining pool. A selfish mining detection plug-in has been developed for the miner's software, allowing one to analyze data patterns coming from a mining pool. As experiments show, the proposed approach outperforms other selfish mining detectors, as it identifies the attacking pool and has lower error rates. The developed solution can be integrated with the miner's software to reduce the negative effects of selfish mining attacks on critical infrastructures such as blockchain-enabled smart cities.

articleTitle: Tracking Robotic Arms with YOLO11 for Smart Automation in Industry 4.0
abstract: The rapid advancement of automation and robotics has become a cornerstone of the smart industry and Industry 4.0, necessitating innovative approaches to enhance operational efficiency and accuracy. In this context, computer vision plays a vital role in monitoring robotic systems, ensuring they perform tasks with precision and reliability. This study employs the YOLO11 algorithm to track the end effector of a robotic arm during pick-and-place operations, simulating industrial environments. Through rigorous experimentation, we observed that YOLO11 demonstrated a high tracking performance, achieving average detection metrics that indicate a strong correlation between commanded and experimental trajectories. The findings highlight that the algorithm can maintain a tracking accuracy above 90%, even during varying movement speeds, thereby reducing the likelihood of operational errors. This research underscores the significance of integrating advanced deep learning techniques into robotic systems, paving the way for enhanced automation capabilities within the framework of Industry 4.0.

articleTitle: Digital Twins and the Problem of Distributed Data Storage
abstract: The article demonstrates the fundamental possibility to solve the problem of digital twins data storage and processing in a distributed digital industrial platform. This problem originates from the fact that a digital twin in the digital economy and Industry 4.0 should be, on the one hand, quickly accessible and on the other hand, properly protected from intentional or unintentional distortions. In the article, we review the variants of digital twin data storage in the conditions of Industry 4.0, and provide the requirements to the data of digital twins. Besides, the requirements for digital twins' data storage systems in the conditions of Industry 4.0 are formulated. Such requirements, in particular, include distributed storage, strong consistency between digital twins' data and the real object, high speed of data processing. The review of modern database management systems belonging to the class of NewSQL solutions is made. The article shows that these solutions can be applied to solve the problem of digital twins distributed data storage in industry 4.0. The direction of further research is defined.

articleTitle: Tire—Road Friction Characteristics Estimation Based on ESO Observer and LSTM Neural Networks
abstract: To enhance the perception of road surface information during autonomous driving, this paper proposes a Tire-Road Friction Characteristics (TRFC) estimation algorithm that integrates a 7-DOF vehicle dynamics model, the Magic Formula, an improved adaptive Extended State Observer (ESO), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks. The vehicle's key state parameters are obtained through the dynamics model, while the tire forces and the ESO observer provide accurate estimates of the utilized TRFC and slip ratio. Furthermore, an improved LSTM model, incorporating the Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) approach based on physical constraints, is employed to estimate the TRFC and critical vehicle state parameters. The algorithm's reliability and robustness are validated through MATLAB/Simulink and CarSim co-simulation experiments. The results demonstrate that the proposed method maintains high accuracy even under highly dynamic and uncertain conditions. This approach can serve as a complementary technique for fusion with vision and LiDAR-based TRFC identification methods, providing theoretical support for improving the safety and stability of autonomous vehicles.

articleTitle: Classification of Objects Based on the Construction of an Enveloping Polygonal Chain for the Highly Automated Vehicles
abstract: This paper presents a method for obstacle recognition and classification using LiDAR data to enhance the operation of highly automated vehicles (HAVs). The approach focuses on constructing an enveloping polygonal chain around a point cloud representation of an obstacle detected by a 3D-LiDAR sensor. The polygonal chain is built using the highest points of the object, and each segment's height difference and angle of inclination relative to the horizon are analyzed. This analysis enables the classification of detected objects into surmountable and insurmountable obstacles, facilitating more efficient and safer route planning for HAVs. Unlike computationally intensive machine learning techniques, this method emphasizes geometric analysis for object classification, ensuring reduced computational overhead and faster processing. Experimental validation on a GAZelle vehicle equipped with an LSLIDAR CH-64 sensor demonstrates the accuracy and reliability of the proposed approach across various obstacle types.

articleTitle: Dual-Stream Attention for Small Object Detection
abstract: This study addresses the challenges of detecting small objects in visually complex environments by utilizing cutting-edge advancements in deep learning. We propose a novel framework which incorporates a dual-stream self-attention mechanism within a multi-head architecture. To further enhance detection precision, our approach employs an innovative output reweighting strategy. The framework is specifically tailored to overcome the limitations of conventional detection models, particularly the difficulty of small objects spanning multiple tokens in feature maps. By adaptively scaling attention across various heads, our method effectively captures intricate details at multiple levels of granularity, significantly improving the identification and localization of small objects. A key component of the proposed model is a softmax-driven reweighting function that prioritizes features essential for object recognition while minimizing irrelevant details and background noise. This targeted refinement not only boosts accuracy but also ensures a more streamlined and efficient detection process. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate that our model surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques in both performance metrics and computational efficiency, making it a scalable solution for real-world applications. Beyond its practical benefits, this work contributes to the theoretical development of attention mechanisms in neural networks, offering new insights into their role in small object detection tasks.

articleTitle: Information and Software Support for the Multifactor Authentication Process using Biometric Data in Linux Kernel-Based Operating Systems
abstract: The article substantiates the necessity of of implementing multifactor authentication based on user biometric data to enhance the security level of computer systems. Traditional methods such as password authentication are not always capable of providing the required level of protection for the account and user data. The authors analyze modern approaches to biometric authentication, identify the advantages of using them within multifactor systems, and address current issues related to the secure storage of biometric data. As a result of their research, they have developed a software architecture that uses the proposed mechanisms for integration in Linux kernel-based operating systems.

articleTitle: Optimization of Micro-Object Identification Based on a Pyramidal Model with Image Segmentation
abstract: A methodology has been developed for optimizing the processes of identification, recognition and classification of micro-objects, pollen grains, unicellular microorganisms, and minerals in rock mass based on the use of properties and characteristics of components in the image structure. Tools for reducing the error in identifying micro-objects are proposed based on filtering defective points using statistical, dynamic, morphometric, geometric, histological, spectral-frequency, and brightness characteristics of the image. The efficiency of the mechanism with the execution of the operation of tracking, detection, correction of defective points, detection of growth dynamics, visual delineation, dynamic approximation, smoothing based on the use of Gaussian, median filtering, Fourier, shift - transformations is investigated. The processes of identifying micro-objects have been optimized based on the alignment of histology sections, finding fragment contours, a set of levels and thresholds, color coding and visualization of micro-objects. A software package for identification, recognition and classification of micro-objects was implemented and software modules were tested on real measurements of cellular elements of the inflammatory series of lung diseases.

articleTitle: Evolution of Technologies: Digital Twins of NPP Power Units, Intelligent NPP Operator Support Systems and the Path to Industry 5.0
abstract: The paper discusses key aspects of the digitalization of nuclear power in the context of the transition to Industry 5.0. The topic's relevance is due to the global transition of world industries to the concept of Industry 5.0, which is focused on integrating digital technologies, strengthening the human-centricity of management services, and increasing their adaptability to new challenges. Particular attention is paid to the use of digital twins and intelligent operator support systems (IOSS) at nuclear power facilities, which transforms their management, considering modern safety, reliability, and efficiency requirements. The paper describes the principles of creating digital twins of NPPs and considers the role of IOSS, the main tasks of which are to increase the level of awareness of NPP operators about the current state of the system, reduce the response time to emergency events, and automate decision-making. The authors propose an algorithm for interacting with a digital twin and IOSS, including collecting and processing data from real systems, modeling in a virtual environment, forecasting scenarios, and recommendations to the operator for optimal control. The algorithm ensures synchronization of the digital model with actual processes, optimization of operating parameters, and increased safety through early detection of deviations. The paper also focuses on the connection of the algorithm with the principles of Industry 5.0.

articleTitle: A Construction of a Sequence of Feedback Controls for Discrete Control Problems Using Asymptotics
abstract: This paper explores the possibility of obtaining a symbolic description of a parametric family of synthesizing controls for nonlinear systems without control constraints using the Padé approximation method and the SDRE-based approach for control synthesis. On an example of a discrete optimal control problem with a positive parameter in the system dynamic equations an algorithm for constructing the first terms of a minimizing sequence of controls is proposed, where each term of the obtained control sequence is represented in the state feedback form. This construction is based on a set of neurons by which we understand various asymptotic approximations, Padé approximations (PA), and functions derived from them. Depending on a particular dynamic system a certain number of neurons will be used to get good quality approximation for the control. Asymptotic approximations and the PAs constructed on their basis capture the qualitative structure of the exact solution. Moreover, PAs can be improved through additional optimization procedures and modifications. The process of neurons selection, or activation, can be interpreted as a reinforcement learning algorithm in a certain neural network.

Author Keywords: approximate parametric family of feedback laws

articleTitle: Optimization of Warehouse Processes Using Machine Learning and Linear Programming
abstract: This paper explores the design of an inventory management model for small warehouses using machine learning and optimization methods. The objective is to develop a system that ensures accurate demand forecasting and automatic calculation of optimal inventory levels, minimizing storage costs and preventing stock shortages. The model incorporates demand forecasting algorithms such as ARIMA, LSTM, and XGBoost, along with inventory optimization methods based on linear programming and genetic algorithms. Special attention is given to integrating an automated inventory replenishment system, as well as monitoring and reporting tools for assessing management efficiency. The proposed model enables companies to reduce operational costs, improve the accuracy and speed of inventory management decision-making, and enhance customer service levels. This work aims to improve inventory management under constrained resources and dynamic market conditions typical of small warehouses.

articleTitle: Studying the Efficiency of Hybrid Algorithms for Fault Detection and Isolation in Navigation Sensors
abstract: Detection and isolation of faults in measurements of navigation sensors is considered. This problem is relevant in the context of autonomous navigation, since in this case, fault-tolerance requirements for the equipment generating navigation solutions are much higher. The paper proposes using both classical techniques based on state observers and machine learning methods. The efficiency of the performance of models based on random forest and recurrent neural network, as well as a hybrid version involving additional data from sliding mode observers are compared. The initial data for training and testing is a generated dataset based on a nonlinear model of a large-capacity vessel motion in the horizontal plane, which takes into account external disturbances, as well as errors of navigation sensors. The class of faults considered is limited to additive faults in the measurement equation.

articleTitle: Proactive Complex Security Analysis of IoT-Based Critical Infrastructure Facilities
abstract: This paper develops an approach for proactive, predictive and complex security analysis of critical infrastructure facilities, that are utilizing Internet of Things technologies (IoT-based CIFs). The study employs extrapolation algorithms and granular computing, which consider the noise present in initial data. This allows even in the uncertainties of data observation and measurement, to determine and predict important aspects of functioning of IoT-based CIFs. We believe that consideration of such knowledge can significantly contribute to the complex security of such systems. The main features of this approach are analyzed. The proposed approach enables proactive security assessment, determining acceptable thresholds for deviations from security requirements. Furthermore, by formalizing these metrics as deviations from security requirements, this approach enables the unification of proactive assessment algorithms. In turn, it opens a possibility for unifying monitoring, protection, and resource management algorithms of IoT-based CIFs.

articleTitle: Methodology for Embedding a Digital Watermark in Java Application Class Files Resistant to Decompilation Attacks Aimed at Its Destruction
abstract: This paper examines the development of a methodology for embedding a digital watermark in class files by replacing bytecode opcodes and adding certain Java programming language constructs that hinder decompilation. The possible actions of an intruder are considered, along with the methods by which an attacker might obtain a class file or a Java application. An analysis of existing decompilers is conducted, with examples of programming language constructs that lead to decompilation errors or incorrect decompilation results. The principle of the methodology is demonstrated, and experiments are conducted to confirm that after embedding the digital watermark using the developed approach, it remains resilient to decompilation attacks aimed at its removal. The compiled class file containing the modified bytecode is analyzed. It is proven that the logic of the Java application remains unchanged after editing the bytecode of the class file and recompiling it. Certain constructs and code design patterns are examined, demonstrating that specific constructs in the source code increases the likelihood of incorrect decompilation of Java application class files, the inability to recompile the decompiled code.

articleTitle: Experience in the Application of Improved Algorithms for Automatic Control of Electrical and Technological Modes in Arc Steelmaking Furnaces
abstract: In this article, a description of the improved control algorithm for RCB burners and injectors of carbon-containing material (CCM) for a modular-type arc steelmaking furnace operating at one of the domestic metallurgical enterprises is presented.
